## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30). Depends on per-owner income routing (sibling) so scoring can evaluate against the acting player's own resources.

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold (using the per-player state model from the competitive state sibling).
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved.

## Out of scope

- Opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- Endless continuation — deferred to a separate top-level issue.
- N-player Monte Carlo — covered by the Monte Carlo harness sibling; architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner) but the initial harness validates head-to-head (1 human vs 1 AI).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic: same seed + same strategy produces identical action sequences; verified by a dedicated deterministic replay test.
- [ ] **AC4:** All existing single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive AI tests (ownership-aware scoring, staff exclusion, determinism).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
- Depends on: competitive state model + income/event routing siblings (per-player resources/score needed for ownership-aware horizon)

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want a competitive state model with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score plus owner-tagged street slots, so the shared street can host multiple owners deterministically via seeded RNG.

## Context

MainStreetState is single-player only (single resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining/finalScore and 10-slot streetGrid of BusinessCard|null). No owner concept exists. This child is the foundation for all competitive layers. Design is parallel per-player (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner, N-player-ready — not a hardcoded 2-player shape, not a single-player shim per producer decision “latter”). The game remains playable without an AI — competitive state is additive; single-player flow is preserved as the 1-player case (N=1).

## Scope

- Introduce per-player state: PlayerRecord (coins, reputation, hand, staff, actionBudget, score) × N; owner-tagged StreetGrid slots (ownerId per slot, null = empty).
- Deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG (same seed → same initial deal).
- Market/decks/incidentDeck remain shared; challenges/activeEffects remain game-scoped unless a rule explicitly scopes them.
- No AI, no income routing, no phase alternation — those are siblings.

## Out of scope

- Per-owner income/event routing (sibling).
- Shared-day phase machine (sibling).
- AI strategy / Monte Carlo (siblings).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 deferred child).
- Endless continuation (deferred to separate top-level issue per producer decision).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** State type exposes per-player resources (coins/reputation), hand, staff, action budget, and score per owner plus owner-tagged street slots; setup creates a deterministic initial state from a seed.
- [ ] **AC2:** Shared market/decks/incidentDeck are unchanged and shared across players.
- [ ] **AC3:** Determinism: same seed produces identical per-player initial state (unit replay test); N=1 behaves identically to the pre-competitive single-player baseline.
- [ ] **AC4:** Resource/slot ownership is addressable by ownerId/owner index in helpers (no single-player shim).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Per-player state types (PlayerRecord[], owner-tagged StreetGrid), setup().
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — Competitive-aware purchase legality helpers (owner-param where needed).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-state.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive state tests (per-player state, determinism, N-player shape).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
- Siblings: shared-day phase, income/event routing, AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038), Monte Carlo harness
- Endless mode: separate top-level issue (deferred per producer decision)

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want a shared-day phase machine where MarketPhases alternate within a day (Option A) and Income/Incident/EndCheck resolve once both players have acted, so competitive turns interleave tightly before shared resolution.

## Context

DayPhase is single-player (DayStart → MarketPhase → InvestmentResolution → IncomePhase → IncidentPhase → EndCheck). No concept of “whose turn within the day” exists. Expected shared-day flow (Option A, confirmed): both players alternate MarketPhases, then shared closing phases run once. This child depends on the competitive state model's active-player tracking.

## Scope

- Shared-day phase machine: active-player index, alternating MarketPhases, then shared Income/Incident/EndCheck.
- Win condition: first player to reach the win threshold wins (confirmed decision).
- Single-player (N=1) unchanged: same sequence with one MarketPhase.
- Diagram shared-day phases in code comment + cover transitions with unit tests.

## Out of scope

- Per-owner income/event routing (sibling — this child's closing phases delegate to that sibling).
- AI strategy / Monte Carlo.
- Endless continuation (deferred to separate top-level issue).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 child).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Shared-day phase machine alternates MarketPhases within a day across N players (active-player tracking), then shared Income/Incident/EndCheck resolve once all players have acted; sequence verified by unit tests including edge cases (action budget hand-off, phase entry/exit invariants).
- [ ] **AC2:** Win condition is first-to-threshold (first player to reach win threshold wins); EndCheck detects the winner correctly.
- [ ] **AC3:** N=1 (single player) preserves the legacy phase sequence with one MarketPhase per day.
- [ ] **AC4:** Phase diagram documented in code comment; transitions covered by unit tests.

- AI strategy / Monte Carlo.
- Endless continuation (deferred).

As a developer/QA, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode (extending MainStreetMonteCarlo) that runs ≥200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics, so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.

## Context

`MainStreetMonteCarlo` is single-player only (`runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` with one strategy × one difficulty per run). Competitive mode needs head-to-head metrics: both players' win/score distributions plus per-player diagnostics. Architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner), but the harness validates the head-to-head (human vs 1 AI) path initially; N>2 extension is a future parameterisation.

## Scope

- Head-to-head harness extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (new entry point or flag): both players act per shared-day, same seed → deterministic head-to-head run.
- ≥200 seeds; outputs win/score distributions plus per-player metrics (wins per owner, average score per owner, draw/early-end handling).
- Single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Out of scope

- AI strategy itself (sibling).
- Per-owner income routing (sibling).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 child).
- Endless continuation (deferred).
- N>2 Monte Carlo — harness is N-player-extensible (numOpponents param) but AC4 validates head-to-head; broader N is a follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Head-to-head harness runs ≥200 seeds with deterministic head-to-head execution (same seed → same per-owner outcome) and produces win/score distributions (win rate per owner, median/average score per owner).
- [ ] **AC2:** Per-player metrics include at least wins, average score, and loss-reason distribution per owner plus a deterministic summary (draw/early-end handling documented).

# Rename the re-roll button to 'Research'

## Problem Statement

The market has a "re-roll" action (button, tooltip, HUD tooltip, help text, in-game messages and activity log) that uses inconsistent, mechanical terminology. This item renames all user-facing "re-roll" / "Refresh Market" strings to the game's "Research" terminology, starting with the market button, while preserving cost visibility and all functional detail.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — "As a player, I want the market action to be called 'Research' everywhere it appears, so that the UI terminology is clear and consistent."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Button label:** The market button text changes from `Re-roll (${refreshCost})` to `Research (${refreshCost})`; the dynamic cost stays visible on the button face.
2. **AC2 — Button tooltip:** The hover tooltip headline is "Invest in researching new opportunities", followed by the existing functional detail (cost, card replacement, Market-phase-only availability, and the disabled reason when inapplicable), with "re-roll" wording changed to "research".
3. **AC3 — Consistent user-facing terminology:** All other user-facing "re-roll" / "Refresh Market" strings are renamed to "Research" terminology:
   - turn-controller instruction messages and activity log (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`),
   - the legality/disabled reason and the market-refresh activity log message (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`),
   - the help-panel "Tools" line (`src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts`),
   - the HUD action tooltip line (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`).
4. **AC4 — No regressions:** The button and action remain fully functional (callback, disabled state, click behaviour, undo/redo, save/load) with no behavioural changes; only strings change.
5. **AC5 — Tests:** Affected tests are updated (notably `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts`, which asserts the help body contains 'refresh market'), and the new button label/tooltip wording is covered so the rename cannot silently regress.
6. **AC6 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, which lists "Market re-roll/refresh").
7. **AC7 — Quality gate:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only user-facing strings, supporting code comments, tests and docs change. No game logic, balance, or data changes.
- The button cost stays visible (`Research (${refreshCost})`) — confirmed by the producer.
- The tooltip keeps the existing functional body and gains the new headline — confirmed by the producer.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — button label `Re-roll (${refreshCost})` (~line 168); tooltip `Pay €${refreshCost} to re-roll the market and replace all visible cards. Removed cards go to their discard piles. Available only during Market phase.${reasonSuffix}` (~line 184); comments mention "Re-roll button" (~lines 146, 148, 158, 182).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — instruction messages `Cannot re-roll: ...` (~287), `Re-rolling the market...` (~293), `Market re-rolled` (~305) and log `Re-rolled market (via UI)` (~306).
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — legality reason `Re-rolling the market is only allowed during MarketPhase.` (~45) and activity log `Re-rolled market (-€${cost}): ...` (~110).
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — help panel line `Refresh Market: re-roll the market row for coins (5, less with the Accountant).` (~138).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — HUD tooltip `No action: re-roll market, sell, end turn. ...` (~118).
- `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` — asserts the help body contains 'refresh market' (line 160); must be updated.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — "Free operations" list contains "Market re-roll/refresh" (~line 277).
- No other test asserts the exact user-facing re-roll strings (checked `refresh-market.test.ts`, `activity-log.test.ts`, `market-extraction-parity.test.ts`).
- The `createActionButton` helper returns a Phaser Container; the label is a `Text` child.

## Desired change

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`: label → `Research (${refreshCost})`; tooltip → `Invest in researching new opportunities.

Pay €${refreshCost} to research the market and replace all visible cards. Removed cards go to their discard piles. Available only during Market phase.${reasonSuffix}`; update the "Re-roll" comments to "Research".
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`: `Cannot re-roll:` → `Cannot research:`; `Re-rolling the market...` → `Researching the market...`; `Market re-rolled` → `Market researched`; `Re-rolled market (via UI)` → `Researched market (via UI)`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`: legality reason → `Researching the market is only allowed during MarketPhase.`; log → `Researched market (-€${cost}): ...`; update comments.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts`: → `Research: research the market row for coins (5, less with the Accountant).`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`: → `No action: research market, sell, end turn. ...`
- Update `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` and any other assertions on the changed strings; add coverage for the button label/tooltip headline (prefer a focused test; if a Phaser render test is brittle, use the repo's static source-guard pattern).
- Update `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — button label, tooltip and comments.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — instruction and log strings.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — legality reason, activity log and comments.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — help-panel "Tools" line.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — HUD tooltip string.
- `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` — update the 'refresh market' assertion.
- `tests/main-street/market-research-button.test.ts` (new, or an existing market-renderer test) — cover label/tooltip wording.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — "Market re-roll/refresh" wording.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Confirmed (Q1):** cost stays visible as `Research (<cost>)` on the button face (producer: "visible").
- **Confirmed (Q2):** the new sentence is the tooltip headline and the existing functional body is retained (producer: "as recommended").
- **Confirmed (Q3):** all user-facing "re-roll"/"Refresh Market" strings are renamed (producer: "everywhere").
- **Risk (related item conflict):** `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` ("Reroll to cost more", plan_complete) AC4 requires the button label/tooltip to report the current escalated cost; keeping the cost in the label preserves that. Coordinate if both land.
- **Risk (test brittleness):** asserting Phaser GameObject internals can be brittle; prefer a static source guard if a render test proves unstable.
- **Risk (missed strings):** "everywhere" could miss a string; mitigation — grep the repo for `re-roll|reroll|Refresh Market` (case-insensitive) at implementation time and after the change.

## Related Work

- `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` — "Reroll to cost more" (open, plan_complete): touches the same button label/tooltip and requires cost visibility; coordinate.
- `CG-0MTKMN7KG006F5EE` — "The cost of a reroll is still 5, it should be 500" (completed): set the flat base cost shown in this label.
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — "Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects" (completed): refresh-cost discounts shown in the label/tooltip.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions and Answers

- **Q:** What should the button label be, and should the cost stay visible on the face of the button?
  - Options: (a) `Research (5)` keep the cost; (b) `Research` cost only in tooltip; (c) other.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — preserves cost visibility and keeps `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` AC4 satisfiable.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-30):** "visible" — option (a) accepted; the cost stays on the button face.
- **Q:** How should the new tooltip text "Invest in researching new opportunities" relate to the existing detailed tooltip?
  - Options: (a) headline plus existing functional detail; (b) replace tooltip entirely with the sentence; (c) sentence plus phase/disabled reason only; (d) other.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — preserves actionable information.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-30):** "as recommended" — option (a) accepted.
- **Q:** Should the rename extend to other user-facing "re-roll"/"Refresh Market" strings, or only the button and its tooltip?
  - Options: (a) only the button and tooltip; (b) also the help panel; (c) all user-facing occurrences; (d) other.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — matches the seed scope, which names only the button and tooltip.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-30):** "everywhere" — option (c) accepted; all user-facing occurrences are renamed (deviates from the recommendation, as chosen by the producer).

Add action-point skills to some staff cards so that hiring them grants the player extra actions per week. The Manager should grant +1 action/week (with its hand-slot bonus reduced to +1), extending the existing General Manager action-economy mechanic down the staff ladder. This adds a second, meaningful build axis (action economy vs. hand capacity) to the staff family.

## Problem statement

The staff family's only differentiating benefit today is hand capacity (`handSlotsAdded`) plus a handful of flat discounts. The General Manager is the sole staff card that grants an extra action per week (`actionsPerTurn: 1`), so the action-economy benefit is confined to a single top-tier card. Players pursuing an action-economy build have no mid-tier staff choices, and the Manager — the most cost-efficient capacity card — competes purely on slots. Granting some staff `actionsPerTurn` gives them a distinct build role and makes the mid-tier ladder a genuine trade-off between capacity and tempo.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants staff choices that support an extra-action-per-week playstyle before the tier-12 General Manager is affordable.
- **Main Street player (mid-game)** — wants the Manager's slot efficiency re-balanced so it is not strictly the best capacity-per-coin pick.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want to hire a Manager that grants +1 action per week (at the cost of one hand slot) so that I can take an extra action each week in the mid game.
- As a Main Street player, I want the staff card tooltip and the Actions HUD tooltip to state the extra-action benefit, so that I understand why my weekly action budget increased.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Manager staff card in `src/card-data.csv` grants `actionsPerTurn: 1` and has `handSlotsAdded` reduced from `2` to `1`, while keeping `cost: 700`, `ongoingCost: 250` and tier 3; its CSV `description` text no longer claims `+2 hand slots` (it states the `+1` hand slot and the `+1` action/week).
2. The Director staff card grants `actionsPerTurn: 1` (retaining `handSlotsAdded: 3`, `cost: 1400`, `ongoingCost: 400`, tier 9), so the ladder is Assistant (capacity) → Manager (+1 action, +1 slot) → Director (+1 action, +3 slots) → Executive (+4 slots).
3. A week-start budget with an employed Manager/Director composes as `1 base + sum(actionsPerTurn) + banked (capped at 2)`, with staff-derived actions consumed first and never banked (existing `MainStreetEngineWeekStart.executeWeekStart` behaviour preserved).
4. The staff card tooltip renders `Actions: +1/week` for the Manager and Director (existing `MainStreetFormatting` staff case), and the Actions HUD tooltip note renders whenever any `actionsPerTurn` staff is employed, with wording that is accurate for Manager/Director (i.e. no longer General-Manager-specific) while still covering the General Manager case.
5. Staff without the ability (Assistant, Apprentice, Socialite, Accountant, Lookout, Executive, and the non-action specialists) are unchanged — no `actionsPerTurn`, no behaviour change.

## Summary

Add a hover tooltip to the persistent synergy lines drawn between adjacent
synergistic businesses on the Main Street board. Hovering a line explains the
shared synergy type and the per-turn effect that link has on each of the two
connected cards.

## User Story

As a Main Street player, I want to hover over a synergy line and see what that
synergy does — the shared type and the coins/reputation each linked business
gains from it — so that I can understand *why* two businesses are connected and
plan my street deliberately, instead of guessing from the line colour alone.

## Problem Statement

The board draws coloured synergy lines between adjacent businesses that share a
synergy type, but the lines are purely decorative: hovering them does nothing.
The player sees that two cards are linked but not which synergy type they share,
the rate that applies, or the value of that specific connection. The only
synergy information available today is the per-card `Synergy: <types>` line in
the business-slot tooltip, which does not explain the link or its magnitude.

## Existing State

- `drawSynergyLines()` in
  `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` draws a
  two-pass `Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics` line (core + glow) per synergy pair and
  adds it to `streetContainer`. The graphics objects are **not interactive** —
  there is no input handler on them.
- `computeSynergyPairs()` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyNeighbors.ts`
  returns `SynergyPair { fromIndex, toIndex, sharedSynergy }`, the data the
  renderer iterates to draw each line. Sold cards still participate as pair
  endpoints (CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ).
- Per-card synergy maths lives in
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`:
  `computeSynergyBonus()` (coin), `computeSynergyRepBonus()` (reputation),
  `effectiveSynergyCoinBonus()` / `effectiveSynergyRepBonus()`. The difficulty
  multiplier is `config.synergyBonusPerNeighbor`.
- Existing formatting helpers live in
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` (`effectiveSynergyRate()`,
  `formatSynergyRate()`, `formatPerTurnReputation()`, `formatCurrency()`).
- Business-slot tooltips already use the shared `TooltipManager`
  (`s.tooltipManager?.show(info, x, y)` / `.hide()`); the manager is created
  only when `!s.replayMode`
  (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`) and already honours the
  `settingsPanel.showTooltips` toggle.

## Desired Change

1. Add a pure, unit-testable content builder — e.g.
   `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo(grid, fromIndex, toIndex, sharedSynergy, config, soldSlots?, gridDims?)`
   in `MainStreetFormatting.ts` — that returns the tooltip text for one link.
2. In `drawSynergyLines()`, give each line a **narrow, invisible interactive hit
   area** (parented into `streetContainer`, drawn/recreated with the rest of the
   street layer) wired to `tooltipManager.show(...)` on `pointerover` and
   `tooltipManager.hide()` on `pointerout`.
3. Guard the wiring the same way existing slot tooltips are: no tooltip in
   `replayMode` and no tooltip when `tooltipManager` is absent; the
   `showTooltips` setting continues to be enforced by `TooltipManager` itself.
4. Ensure the hit area does not swallow the existing business-slot hover/click
   interactions except immediately along the line (see Constraints).

### Suggested tooltip format (implementation may refine wording)

```
Food synergy
Bakery  ⟷  Diner
Bakery: +2 coins/turn from this link
Diner: +1 coins/turn from this link
+5 reputation/turn  (only when a reputation-synergy contribution exists)
```

Sold endpoints are called out explicitly, e.g.
`Bakery (sold): earns nothing, but still anchors this synergy`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hovering a persistent synergy line shows a tooltip that names the shared
  synergy type and states the per-turn coin and/or reputation effect of that
  link for **each** endpoint, computed with the active difficulty multiplier
  (`config.synergyBonusPerNeighbor`).
- The tooltip is hidden when the pointer leaves the line, and is not shown at
  all in replay mode; the existing `settingsPanel.showTooltips = false` toggle
  suppresses it (via `TooltipManager`).
- A sold endpoint is represented correctly: it earns nothing from the link
  itself, while the link still anchors synergy for the other endpoint, and the
  tooltip says so.
- The line hover hit area does not break the existing business-slot
  interactions: slot hover tooltips, click-to-place, sell, and upgrade
  targeting continue to work everywhere except the line's immediate vicinity.
- Unit tests cover the pure `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo()` builder (shared
  type, coin-only, reputation, sold endpoint, zero-synergy opt-out, difficulty
  multiplier) and an automated test covers the hover wiring on a rendered line.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the shared `TooltipManager` (`@ui`) — do **not** add a bespoke tooltip
  renderer, consistent with
  [Standardize TooltipManager across all games] (CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44) and
  [Tooltip single-source fix] (CG-0MTJP6RNL008LGF3).
- Keep the content builder **pure** (no Phaser/scene dependency) so it can be
  unit-tested headless, mirroring `synergyLineEndpoints.ts`.
- Synergy lines are drawn **after** the slot rectangles in `drawSynergyLines()`,
  so their hit areas sit on top of the slot hit zones. The hit area must be
  narrow (a thin band around the segment, thick enough for a mouse but not so
  thick that it steals slot hover) and the chosen thickness/approach must be
  documented in a code comment.
- Hit areas are recreated on every `streetContainer` rebuild (the street layer
  is rebuilt by `refreshAll()`), so their creation must not leak listeners or
  leave stale objects behind.
- Reduced-motion: no animation is introduced; the tooltip appears/hides
  immediately, so reduced-motion preferences are unaffected.
- No new engine-level (`src/`) API is expected — Main Street-local formatting +
  renderer wiring only.
- Out of scope: tooltips on the transient synergy-formation animation line,
  changing the synergy formula, and changing line geometry/colours.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — Add an
  interactive hit area per synergy pair inside `drawSynergyLines()` and wire it
  to `s.tooltipManager`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — New pure
  `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo()` builder (shared synergy type + per-endpoint
  coin/reputation effect).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — Reuse/extract the
  per-link contribution maths if a per-neighbour share helper is needed
  (avoid duplicating the synergy formula).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyNeighbors.ts` — Source of
  `SynergyPair`; may need no change beyond typing.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-tooltip.test.ts` — New unit tests for the content
  builder.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-tooltip.browser.test.ts` — New browser test for
  hover wiring (or extend `tests/main-street/synergy-visuals.test.ts`).
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — Document the synergy-line tooltip
  interaction.
- `example-games/main-street/README.md` — Mention the tooltip in the synergy
  overview (if the README describes synergy lines).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption (documented, producer may adjust):** "the effect of that synergy"
  means the shared type plus the per-link per-turn coin/reputation contribution
  for each endpoint, rather than a generic rules paragraph. The suggested
  format above is a proposal; wording can change without altering the ACs.
- **Risk — per-link vs. card-total mismatch:** `computeSynergyBonus()` rounds
  the *total* across all matching neighbours, so a per-link share may not sum
  exactly to the displayed card total. The tooltip must not imply a precision
  it does not have; document the chosen presentation (per-link share formatted
  to at most one decimal, or card total) in the builder's doc comment.
- **Risk — input interception:** adding interactive objects on top of the slot
  hit zones can regress slot hover/click. Mitigation: narrow hit band + an
  explicit regression test for slot hover/click; keep the band culled with the
  line.
- **Risk — re-render churn:** `drawSynergyLines()` runs on every refresh; a
  fresh hit area per refresh must be destroyed with the container or it leaks.
- **Scope-creep guard:** any desire to also tooltip the *animated* formation
  line, restyle lines, or change synergy values must be filed as a separate
  work item, not folded into this one.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MM4REC2Z0GS2YKT** – Main Street: PRD Milestone 2 -- Full Content and Crafting/Building System (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHCJJ5009AB4X** – Fix Lighting Spike scene visibility (completed)
- **CG-0MQOBJ9BW006TTJR** – Main Street score tooltip should show calculation breakdown (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)
- `example-games/gym/README.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)

### Manual related references

- **CG-0MQQHBZ3D002J02E** – Add visual synergy lines between adjacent businesses
  (completed): introduced the lines this work item makes interactive.
- **CG-0MSVM3WCD007BRQP** – Synergy lines drawn edge-to-edge / corner-to-corner
  (completed): `synergyLineEndpoints.ts` geometry reused for the hit band.
- **CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ** – Main Street sold businesses still provide synergy
  (completed): defines sold-endpoint semantics the tooltip must reflect.
- **CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44** – Standardize TooltipManager across all games
  (completed): the shared tooltip component to reuse.
- **CG-0MTJP6RNL008LGF3** – Tooltip single-source fix (completed): tooltip
  content should come from shared formatters.
- **CG-0MT5Y9AD2001MKWZ** – Tooltips on businesses are confusing (completed):
  precedent for clarifying Main Street tooltip wording.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — synergy line visual/audio spec
  (lines, coin flights, animation) to extend with the tooltip.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was required: the seed context and the existing
Main Street code path (`drawSynergyLines` → `SynergyPair` → per-card synergy
formula → `TooltipManager`) were sufficient to draft a clear brief. The single
open design decision was resolved by documented assumption:

- **Assumption A1 (tooltip content):** the tooltip shows the shared synergy
  type and the per-link per-turn coin/reputation contribution for each
  endpoint, rather than a generic rules sentence. Rationale: this matches the
  wording "showing the effect of that synergy" and the precedent set by
  [Add scoring tooltip to expedition column headers] (CG-0MLXCSSES11VPL3C),
  which surfaces the live contribution rather than a definition. Source:
  repo evidence (`SynergyPair.sharedSynergy`, `computeSynergyBonus`,
  `computeSynergyRepBonus`). **OPEN QUESTION for the producer:** confirm the
  proposed format, or specify an alternative (e.g. show the card's *total*
  synergy bonus instead of the per-link share).

# Intake Brief — Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M)

The `staff-it` (IT Specialist) and `staff-delivery` (Delivery Driver) descriptions advertise coin-cost reductions that no engine path applies. They were rescaled to the ×100 integer economy in `CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC` but deliberately left unimplemented there (Q4 decision), because their wording named a per-business target that has no implementing mechanic. This item decides the intended scope (street-wide, confirmed by the producer) and implements both effects end-to-end.

## Problem statement

The two cards promise a discount the engine never applies, so the printed ability is not the ability the player gets. This item removes that text/data gap by backing each description with a data column and an engine consumer, and by extending the staff cost-text regression guard so the gap cannot silently return.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — reads a staff card's printed ability and expects the advertised reduction to apply where the engine charges the cost.
- **Game designer / balancer** — needs every staff cost-reduction description backed by a `card-data.csv` data column so economy tuning is trustworthy.
- **Developer / QA** — needs the regression guard to fail loudly if a staff cost-reduction description is not backed by data.

### User stories

- As a player, when I employ the IT Specialist I pay 100 less when I refresh the market.
- As a player, when I employ the Delivery Driver I pay 50 less when I buy a business card.
- As a designer, every staff cost-reduction description is backed by a data column and an engine consumer.
- As a developer, the guard fails with the offending card id if a description and its data column drift apart.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **IT Specialist refresh discount is implemented and data-backed.** `src/card-data.csv` sets `refreshCostDiscount = 100` for `staff-it` and its description reads street-wide (e.g. "Modernizes operations. Reduces market refresh cost by 100."). With a hired IT Specialist, `refreshMarketCost(state)` equals `REFRESH_MARKET_COST - 100`; with an IT Specialist **and** an Accountant it equals `- 200`; the result is floored at 0. Verified by unit tests.
2. **Delivery Driver purchase discount is implemented and data-backed.** A new `purchaseCostDiscount` staff field and `card-data.csv` column carry `50` for `staff-delivery`; the parser populates it onto `StaffCard`; its description reads street-wide (e.g. "Handles the logistics. Reduces business card purchase cost by 50."). While a Delivery Driver is hired, the coin cost of acquiring/placing a business or community-space card is reduced by 50 through **all** acquisition paths — `purchaseBusiness` (click, listed cost), `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (drag: discount the base cost **then** apply the +50% premium), and `playBusinessFromHand` (deferred listed payment, including the same-week composite premium) — while `moveToHand` (0 coins) is unaffected. Effective cost is floored at 0; multiple `purchaseCostDiscount` staff stack additively. Verified by unit tests.
3. **Regression guard extended.** `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` registers `staff-it` with `column: 'refreshCostDiscount'` and `staff-delivery` with `column: 'purchaseCostDiscount'` (both non-null, `UNIMPLEMENTED_NOTE` removed), and the description-amount == data-column assertions pass.
4. **New column is schema-coordinated (cross-repo).** The `purchaseCostDiscount` column is added to core `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` (`CsvRow`, `CSV_COLUMNS`, `NUMERIC_COLUMNS`), to the `card-data.csv` header (immediately after `upgradeCostDiscount`, before `art_notes`), to the staff parser, and the `tce-main-street` `./core` submodule pin is bumped; `balance-cards-csv-pipeline.test.ts` column-count/order assertions are updated and pass.
5. **AI affordability parity.** `MainStreetAiStrategy` uses the effective (discounted) business-purchase cost for its affordability/value scoring, so AI play is not disadvantaged. Verified by a unit test.
6. **Documentation updated.** `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (ability/description/rationale cells) removes the "description-only — effect not implemented (gap)" notes and reflects the implemented mechanics; `docs/main-street/specialization-skills.md` records the implemented cost-reduction mechanics. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Determinism preserved.** No new RNG consumption; headless/AI parity and seeded determinism are unchanged. Verified by the existing determinism tests plus any new tests.
8. **Tests, build and full suite green.** New/updated unit tests pass, `npm run build` succeeds, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Source of truth is `card-data.csv`.** Do not hand-rebalance unrelated values.
- **Scoping is street-wide (confirmed).** `refreshCostDiscount` is already summed street-wide by `refreshMarketCost`; `purchaseCostDiscount` is summed street-wide across hired staff (`state.staffCards`), matching `refreshCostDiscount` and the Negotiator skill. Do not silently make either effect per-business.
- **Pricing precedence.** For the discounted +50% buy-and-place composite, discount the listed base cost first, then apply the premium (the rule established by `CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC`).
- **CSV schema addition is cross-repo.** A new column requires a core (`Tableau-Card-Engine`) `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` change plus a `tce-main-street` `./core` submodule pin bump, mirroring the `upgradeCostDiscount` precedent (`MS-0MULW540X009EP9A`).
- **No new RNG consumption; determinism and headless/AI parity preserved.**
- **Minimal churn** — touch only the staff/economy paths in scope.

### Out of scope

- Rebalancing any other coin/reputation value.
- Implementing the other nominal applicant perks (Barista, Bookkeeper, Customer Service Rep, Security Guard, etc.) — their live effects come from the random specialization-skill system (`CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK`).
- Changing the base `REFRESH_MARKET_COST` or introducing escalating re-roll pricing (tracked separately in `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`).

## Existing state

- `staff-it` (`src/card-data.csv`): `cost=800`, `tier=4`, `ongoingCost=100`, `allowedBusinessTypes=Commerce|Entertainment|Service`, description "Modernizes operations. Reduces this business refresh cost by 100." — **no** `refreshCostDiscount` value.
- `staff-delivery` (`src/card-data.csv`): `cost=300`, `tier=2`, `ongoingCost=50`, `allowedBusinessTypes=Food|Commerce`, description "Handles the logistics. Reduces business card purchase cost by 50 for this business." — no matching data column exists.
- `refreshMarketCost(state)` (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`) is a single global re-roll of the one-row market (`REFRESH_MARKET_COST = 500`); it sums every hired staff card's `refreshCostDiscount` (street-wide) plus the Negotiator skill (`skill-negotiator`, −100) and clamps at 0. There is **no per-business refresh**.
- `purchaseBusiness` (click, listed cost), `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (drag, `Math.ceil(cost * 1.5 * 2) / 2`), and `playBusinessFromHand` (deferred listed cost, optional premium) charge `card.cost` directly; there is no purchase-cost-discount field or path. `moveToHand` costs 0 coins.
- `computeUpgradeCostDiscount(state, slotIndex)` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`) is the established per-business discount helper (Financial Advisor `upgradeCostDiscount`), applied in the upgrade acquisition paths.
- `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` currently registers both cards with `column: null` and `UNIMPLEMENTED_NOTE`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` marks both cards "description-only — effect not implemented (gap)".

## Desired change

- Set `refreshCostDiscount = 100` on `staff-it` in `card-data.csv`; reword its description to street-wide wording. No engine change is required — `refreshMarketCost` already consumes the column.
- Add a `purchaseCostDiscount` staff field, `card-data.csv` column and parser support; set `50` on `staff-delivery`; reword its description to street-wide wording.
- Add a pure `computePurchaseCostDiscount(state)` helper in `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` (street-wide sum over `state.staffCards`, clamped at 0) and apply the effective cost in `canPurchaseBusiness`/`purchaseBusiness`, `buyAndPlaceBusiness`, and `playBusinessFromHand` (discount the base cost before any premium).
- Update `MainStreetAiStrategy` to score/afford business purchases using the discounted cost.
- Add/extend unit tests for both effects (click, drag, deferred play-from-hand, stacking, clamp, discount-then-premium, AI parity), and extend the regression guard to non-null column contracts for both cards.
- Coordinate the new column across the game CSV and core balance-cards schema; bump the `./core` pin.
- Update `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and `docs/main-street/specialization-skills.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — `staff-it` gains `refreshCostDiscount=100`; `staff-delivery` gains `purchaseCostDiscount=50`; both descriptions reworded street-wide.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — add `readonly purchaseCostDiscount?: number` to `StaffCard`.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — parse the `purchaseCostDiscount` staff column into templates.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — add pure `computePurchaseCostDiscount(state)` (mirrors `refreshCostDiscount` aggregation/floor semantics).
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — `refreshMarketCost` (no logic change expected for the IT Specialist).
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — apply the purchase discount in `canPurchaseBusiness` / `purchaseBusiness`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketHand.ts` — apply the discount in `playBusinessFromHand` (base before premium).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — apply the discount in `buyAndPlaceBusiness` (base before premium).
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — use the effective (discounted) business-purchase cost for affordability/value scoring.
- `core/src/balance-cards/csv.ts` — add `purchaseCostDiscount` to `CsvRow` / `CSV_COLUMNS` / `NUMERIC_COLUMNS` (core repo), then bump the `./core` pin.
- `tests/main-street/staff-cost-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — non-null `column` contracts for both cards; drop `UNIMPLEMENTED_NOTE`.
- `tests/main-street/` — new/updated tests for both effects (click + drag + deferred play-from-hand, stacking, clamp, discount-then-premium, AI parity).
- `tests/main-street/balance-cards-csv-pipeline.test.ts` — update column-count/order assertions.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — update the staff ability/description/rationale cells and remove the "gap" notes.
- `docs/main-street/specialization-skills.md` — note the implemented cost-reduction mechanics.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC** (core, in_review) — Staff effects adjusted for the ×100 coin values; Q4 deferred IT Specialist / Delivery Driver implementation and corrected their text only. This item is the explicit follow-up.
- **MS-0MULW540X009EP9A** (completed) — CSV schema: add `upgradeCostDiscount` column; the cross-repo precedent for adding a staff discount column.
- **MS-0MULWC8CR0011NOX** (completed) — Financial Advisor end-to-end: per-business discount helper and all upgrade acquisition paths.
- **MS-0MULWEEE8007J2TB** (completed) — Accountant `refreshCostDiscount` fixed to ×100; the refresh-discount precedent.
- **MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z** (completed) — staff description text ×100 consistency; created the guard this item extends.
- **MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ** (open) — "Reroll to cost more": changes `refreshMarketCost` semantics (escalating base) and interacts with the IT Specialist refresh discount. Coordinate if both land together.
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** (in-progress) — sibling staff-ability implementation touching the same CSV, catalog and guard; sequence to avoid merge conflicts.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: cross-repo schema desynchronisation** if the new column is added without the core `csv.ts` + submodule pin update. Mitigation: one coordinated change, per `MS-0MULW540X009EP9A`.
- **Risk: scoping leak / bypass.** If the purchase discount is applied only to click+drag, a player could bypass it by moving a card to hand and playing it later. Mitigation: apply it consistently across `purchaseBusiness`, `buyAndPlaceBusiness` and `playBusinessFromHand`; assert the scope boundary in tests.
- **Risk: drag-premium ordering** changes the price. Mitigation: discount the base cost, then apply the premium, and assert in tests.
- **Risk: AI ignores the discount.** Mitigation: update `MainStreetAiStrategy` affordability/value to use the effective cost.
- **Risk: scope creep.** Keep to these two cards only.
- **Risk: ordering conflict with `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`** (escalating re-roll). Mitigation: coordinate sequencing; the IT discount applies to whatever the escalated base cost is.
- **Assumption:** multiple `purchaseCostDiscount` staff stack additively and clamp at 0, mirroring `refreshCostDiscount` / `upgradeCostDiscount`. (Confirmed street-wide.)
- **Assumption:** the description amounts (100 / 50) are correct on the ×100 scale and are not rebalanced here.
- **Assumption:** `playBusinessFromHand` is included in the Delivery Driver scope (deferred payment for a business card is economically a purchase); `moveToHand` costs 0 coins and is excluded. This closes the move-to-hand bypass. Documented for the implementer; the producer may narrow it if desired.

## Design decisions (confirmed)

- **IT Specialist — street-wide refresh discount (option a).** Reuse `refreshCostDiscount = 100` on `staff-it`; reword the description to remove "this business". No new engine surface.
- **Delivery Driver — street-wide purchase discount (option a).** Add `purchaseCostDiscount = 50`, applied street-wide to business/community-space purchases (click + drag, base-then-premium, plus deferred play-from-hand for consistency); reword the description.
- **Description/catalog/guard/schema (option a).** Reword both descriptions to street-wide, back both with data columns, and coordinate the new column across game + core.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (IT Specialist, prior session): "Reuse `refreshCostDiscount = 100` on `staff-it` (street-wide; stacks with Accountant/Negotiator) and reword, or introduce a new per-business refresh mechanic?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "(1) A — reuse `refreshCostDiscount = 100`, street-wide."** Source: interactive reply in this session. Research: `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` `refreshMarketCost` sums `refreshCostDiscount` street-wide; `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` has `computeRefreshCostDiscount` (Negotiator −100); `staff-accountant` already uses `refreshCostDiscount=100`; parent `CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC` Q4.
- Q2 (Delivery Driver, prior session): "Add `purchaseCostDiscount = 50` applied street-wide to business/community-space purchases (click + drag, base-then-premium) and reword, or scope to adjacency, or leave unimplemented?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "(2) a — add `purchaseCostDiscount = 50`, street-wide, click + drag, base-then-premium."** Source: interactive reply. Research: no `purchaseCostDiscount` reference exists in `src/` or `tests/`; `purchaseBusiness`/`buyAndPlaceBusiness`/`playBusinessFromHand` charge `card.cost` directly; parent `CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC` Q4.
- Q3 (description/catalog/guard/schema, prior session): "Reword to street-wide, back both descriptions with columns, and coordinate the new column across game + core?" — **Answer (producer, interactive): "(3) a — reword to street-wide, back both descriptions with data columns, coordinate the new column across game + core."** Source: interactive reply. Research: the guard currently registers both cards with `column: null` + `UNIMPLEMENTED_NOTE`; adding a CSV column requires core `src/balance-cards/csv.ts` + `./core` pin coordination (precedent `MS-0MULW540X009EP9A`).
- Prior context (parent, `CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC` Q4): IT Specialist and Delivery Driver were deferred from the ×100 migration because their per-business target had no implementing mechanic; their descriptions were rescaled but their effects left unimplemented. This item closes that gap under the street-wide decisions above.

# Storyline model & extraction seam

**Goal (user story).** As a content designer, I want to declare storyline membership and multi-way options in card data, and as a developer I want the definition/state/resolution behind a small game-agnostic seam, so the mechanic can grow and later move to the core engine without rewriting callers.

Second child of the "write storylines" epic (MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV), building on the regression harness in C1.

## Scope

- Optional `storylineId` + `storylineTitle` on `EventCard` (and the CSV), parsed by `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts`; absent fields preserve today's behaviour.
- A generalised ordered option model: each option has a label, a successor card id (nullable = end) and an effect policy (`apply` | `skip`). The legacy `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` representation remains byte-for-byte equivalent (compiled to the same two options).
- An extraction seam: storyline definition, `PendingEventChoice` state and resolution exposed through a small interface/registry with pure functions, documented for later movement into the core engine. Corners may be cut, but callers must not reach into Main-Street-only internals.

## Acceptance Criteria

# Reduce time upcoming event is shown

## Problem statement

During the end-of-turn routine an incident card from the Upcoming queue is revealed at board centre and held face-up for 4 seconds (`4000ms`). That hold is longer than needed: once the coin/reputation delta bubbles have finished animating, the extra wait only delays the turn. The hold should be shortened to **1 second longer than the delta-bubble animation** (target ≈ 1920ms).

## Users

- **Main Street player**: Needs the incident card shown long enough to read it and see the coin/reputation delta bubbles land, but not so long that the end-of-turn routine drags. Example user story: *As a player, I want the Upcoming incident reveal to finish shortly after its coin/reputation bubbles land, so the next turn starts promptly without me losing the ability to read the incident.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Shortened hold (full motion)**: `animateIncidentReveal` holds the face-up incident card for `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS` = **1920ms** — i.e. 1 second longer than the 920ms delta-bubble animation (600ms flight + 4 × 80ms max stagger) — replacing the previous 4000ms.
2. **Reduced motion parity**: the reduced-motion path uses the same `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS` value; no duplicate hardcoded duration remains.
3. **No hang / exactly-once completion**: the `onComplete` callback still fires exactly once after the shortened hold + return animation, and the turn-advance chain is never left pending.
4. **Bubbles complete before the hold ends**: the delta-bubble animation window (max 5 bubbles × 80ms stagger + 600ms flight = 920ms) finishes before the hold elapses, so bubbles are never cut off.
5. **Single named constant**: the duration is defined once in `MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` as a named constant, with the bubble flight/stagger values it derives from; no literal `4000` remains for the reveal hold.
6. **Testing/validation**: unit tests assert the new hold duration and the constant relationship (`hold = flights + stagger × (maxBubbles − 1) + 1000`); the incident-reveal browser test's timing expectations are updated to the shortened choreography.
7. **Documentation updated**: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full suite green**: the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Turn-advance chain preserved**: the shortened hold must still fire `onComplete` exactly once; the turn must never hang or double-advance.
- **Bubble readability**: the new hold must not truncate the delta-bubble animation (target 1920ms > 920ms bubble window).
- **Reduced-motion preserved**: reduced-motion players must still get a readable hold (no flight/flip/bubbles, but the hold remains) — per the original design (CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I).
- **Replay/headless unchanged**: replay mode remains a no-op that still fires `onComplete`.
- **No incident**: when no incident resolves, the animation stays a complete no-op (no delay added).

## Existing state

- `MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` → `animateIncidentReveal()` contains the hold as a hardcoded `4000` in two places:
  - the reduced-motion path (`s.time.delayedCall(4000, () => { cleanup(); })`), and
  - the full-motion path (after the hinge flip: `s.time.delayedCall(4000, () => { … return animation … })`).
- `animateIncidentDeltaBubbles()` launches up to 5 bubbles per resource at `i * 80ms` with a `600ms` flight — a 920ms window — using local `flightMs = 600` and literal `80` staggers.
- Nominal full choreography today: flight 550ms + hinge 260ms + hold 4000ms + return 400ms ≈ 5210ms.
- The reveal blocks the day start until the hold completes (`MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.finishTurnPresentation`).

## Desired change

1. Introduce a named hold constant (e.g. `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS`) in `MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts`, derived from the bubble animation: 600ms flight + 4 × 80ms stagger + 1000ms buffer = **1920ms**. Extract the bubble flight/stagger literals into named constants so the relationship is explicit and the hold cannot silently drift shorter than the bubble window.
2. Replace both hardcoded `4000` hold delays in `animateIncidentReveal()` with the new constant (full-motion and reduced-motion paths share it).
3. Update the incident-reveal unit and browser tests to the shortened choreography (including the "4000ms hold" assertions and timing-margin comments).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` — replace the two hardcoded `4000` hold delays in `animateIncidentReveal()`; extract the `600`/`80` bubble literals in `animateIncidentDeltaBubbles()` into named constants.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — add `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS` (≈1920ms) plus `INCIDENT_BUBBLE_FLIGHT_MS` (600) and `INCIDENT_BUBBLE_STAGGER_MS` (80), with a derivation comment.
- `tests/main-street/incident-reveal-animator.test.ts` — update the `delay >= 4000` hold assertions to the new constant; add an assertion tying the hold to the bubble window.
- `tests/main-street/incident-reveal.browser.test.ts` — update the choreography timing notes/margins to the shortened hold.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I** (completed, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Upcoming card reveal in end-of-turn routine*: introduced the 4-second hold and bubble choreography this item shortens; its "timing is fixed: 4 seconds" constraint is deliberately superseded here.
- **CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q** (completed, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Don't add coins/reputation/score until the end of the end-of-turn cycle*: owns the deferred-mutation / deferred HUD window that the reveal's `pendingDeltas` participates in.
- **CG-0MUA1UH3A008M4BS** (in_review, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Reputation and coins from Upcoming should flow in the correct direction*: owns Upcoming delta routing (attached vs HUD) and the coin/reputation flights referenced by this item.
- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** (completed, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Income Phase: phased card-effect animations*: the phased income choreography that runs before the reveal.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption** — "the animation for the coins and reputation" means the delta-bubble animation during the reveal hold (600ms flight + up to 4 × 80ms stagger = 920ms), confirmed by the operator. Target hold = 920ms + 1000ms = **1920ms**.
- **Assumption** — the reduced-motion path keeps the same 1920ms hold (rather than being shortened to ~1000ms with no bubbles), preserving readable time per the original design. Revisit with the producer only if a shorter reduced-motion hold is wanted.
- **Risk** — if the bubble count or stagger changes later, a hardcoded 1920ms could truncate the animation; mitigated by deriving the constant from the bubble flight/stagger constants.
- **Risk** — timing-based tests are brittle; the unit test should assert against the constant (not a magic number) where practical, and browser tests keep generous margins.
- **Risk** — shortening the hold interacts with the deferred HUD window and the incident-reveal → day-start chain; the exactly-once `onComplete` guarantee must be preserved.
- **Scope-creep risk** — requests to change the flight/hinge/return durations or add new reveal effects are out of scope and must be raised as separate work items.

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- **Q1**: The description says "Reduce this to 1 second longer than the animation for the coins and reputation". Which animation is the reference point?
  - Options presented: (1) the delta-bubble animation during the incident hold (~920ms = 600ms flight + 4 × 80ms max stagger) → target ≈ 1920ms; (2) the coin flight duration (`INCOME_FLIGHT_MS` = 600ms) → target ≈ 1600ms.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive): Option 1** — the delta-bubble animation time, target hold ≈ 1920ms.
  - Evidence: `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` (`animateIncidentDeltaBubbles`, `flightMs = 600`, stagger `i * 80`).
- **Q2** (resolved by repo inspection, no operator input needed): Where is the hold implemented and how long is it? — `animateIncidentReveal()` hardcodes `4000` in both the full-motion and reduced-motion paths. Source: code inspection.

# Problem Statement

When using the developer cheat menu (Market Card Cheat) to replace a card in the market slot, the replacement card cannot be taken — the HUD shows "No affordable cards" and the card is not interactive.

# Users

- **Developer testers**: The cheat menu is a development/debugging tool used by the development team to test game scenarios quickly.

**User story**: As a developer tester, I want to add any card to the market via the cheat menu and immediately be able to take/buy that card, so that I can test game scenarios without being blocked by the card being unresponsive.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **Cheat-placed cards are clickable**: After using the Market Card Cheat menu to replace a market slot with a card, clicking the card successfully moves it to the player's hand (no unresponsive card).
2. **Cheat card appears in affordability summary**: The card appears in the "Can buy:" HUD summary (e.g., "Can buy: 1 business") alongside other affordable cards of the same family.
3. **All card families work**: The fix works for all card families supported by the cheat menu (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff).
4. **Existing cheat functionality preserved**: Filtering, searching, and replacing market cards continue to work as before.

# Constraints

- The fix must be surgical — only modify the `cheatReplaceMarketCard` function in `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`.
- Cheat-generated cards already have unique IDs (`${templateId}--cheat-${nonce}`) and reset properties (level, incomeBonus, etc.) — `family` should follow the same explicit-set pattern.
- The fix must not affect production gameplay — the cheat menu is strictly a dev/debug tool.

# Existing state

- **Card templates** in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` are typed as `Omit<BusinessCard, 'family' | 'level' | 'incomeBonus' | 'synergyRangeBonus' | 'reputationBonus'>[]` — the `family` field is intentionally **omitted** from templates (it is inferred from the array source).
- **`cheatReplaceMarketCard`** in `MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` creates cheat cards by spreading the template:
  ```typescript
  const newCard: AnyCard = { ...(template as any), id: `${baseId}--cheat-${cheatNonce++}` } as AnyCard;
  ```
  The function explicitly resets `level`, `incomeBonus`, etc. for business/community-space cards, but **does not explicitly set `family`** — leaving it as `undefined`.
- **Market rendering** in `MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` determines click handlers by checking `card.family`:
  ```typescript
  if (card.family === 'business' || card.family === 'community-space') {
      s.onBusinessCardClick(card as BusinessCard);
  } else if (card.family === 'upgrade') { ... }
  ```
  When `card.family` is `undefined`, none of these conditions match, so the cheat card is not interactive.
- **Affordability check** in `MainStreetMarketUtils.ts` also filters by family:
  ```typescript
  c => (c.family === 'business' || c.family === 'community-space') && c.cost <= state.resourceBank.coins
  ```
  The `undefined` family fails this check, so the card is not shown as "affordable".

# Desired change

Explicitly set the `family` property on cheat-created cards to match the card's actual family, so that rendering and affordability checks work correctly.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — `cheatReplaceMarketCard` function, where the new card is created (fix location)
- `src/MainStreetMarketUtils.ts` — `getAffordableBusinessCards`, `getAffordableUpgradeCards` (affordability checks that depend on `family`)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — `refreshMarket` (rendering that routes click handlers by `family`)
- `src/debug/MarketCardCheatOverlay.ts` — `MarketCardCheatOverlay` (invokes the cheat function, already passes correct `family`)

# Related work

- **WL-0MUH5HU580064VMR** — "Show which cards are in the current deck in the market cards cheat" (related cheat menu feature, separate work item)

# Risks & Assumptions

# Ship a Playable Web Copy of Main Street (GitHub Pages)

**Work item:** MS-0MUQ1KXAS003FJ42 · `feature` · `critical`

**Headline.** Add an automated GitHub Pages pipeline to `tce-main-street` so
that every ship (`dev → main`) publishes a tested, playable web copy of the
launcher containing only Main Street (plus the core-owned Gym), at
`https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/`.

## Problem statement

When `tce-main-street` is shipped (`dev` merged to `main`) there is **no automated
web deployment**. The Tableau-Card-Engine core publishes its multi-game web
launcher to GitHub Pages on every push to `main`
(`https://thewizardscode.github.io/Tableau-Card-Engine/`), but the single-game
Main Street repo has no `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, no Pages configuration,
and its Vite build uses `base: '/'`, which resolves assets to the wrong path
under a project Pages URL (`/tce-main-street/`) and would 404.

## Users

- **Player / prospective buyer** — wants to play Main Street in a browser without
  cloning the repo or installing a desktop build:
  *"As a player, I visit the published URL and can start playing Main Street
  immediately, with all art and audio loading."*
- **Release producer** — wants each release to publish a verified, playable
  web artefact automatically, with the same quality gates as desktop/repo
  releases:
  *"As a producer, when `dev` is promoted to `main` I want the web build to be
  tested, built and published with no manual steps."*
- **Game developer** — wants a reproducible CI build they can inspect when a
  release misfires:
  *"As a developer, I can see the workflow run and the uploaded Pages artefact
  for any release."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **1.** **Auto-deploy on ship** — every push to `main` runs a GitHub Actions workflow
   that builds `tce-main-street` and deploys `dist/` to GitHub Pages at
   `https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/`.
- **2.** **Main Street only (with launcher)** — the published site shows the launcher /
   game-selector UI containing exactly one playable example game, **Main Street**
   (plus the core-owned Gym, which is always present). No other `tce-<game>`
   appears.
- **3.** **Assets resolve under the Pages base path** — the bundled JS/CSS entry, card
   art, and audio load with no 404s when served from `/tce-main-street/`
   (verified by a smoke/browser check against the production build).
- **4.** **Gated deployment** — the workflow runs unit tests and the production build
   first; a failing test or build blocks deployment (no artefact published).
- **5.** **No stored SSH credentials** — the build composes the `./core` submodule from
   the public core repo over HTTPS; the workflow needs no repository SSH secrets.
- **6.** **Documented setup & verification** — first-time Pages setup (Settings → Pages
   → Source: GitHub Actions) and the release/verification steps are documented in
   the repo.
- **7.** **Testing/validation criterion** — an automated check (e.g. `vite preview`
   under the Pages base plus a Playwright smoke assertion, or a dedicated
   build-output test) confirms the deployed base path serves the app entry point
   and Main Street boots.
- **8.** **Documentation updated** — all related documentation is updated to reflect
   the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.
- **9.** **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Auto on `main`:** the trigger is a push to `main`; the ship skill's
  `dev → main` merge therefore publishes with no extra ship-skill change.
  Agents must never push to `main` directly outside the ship workflow.
- **Public repo, HTTPS only:** the workflow may not rely on SSH keys or other
  secrets; `core` (and any composed repo) is public.
- **Generated Vite config:** `vite.config.ts` is auto-generated by
  `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`; a base-path fix that only lives in
  `vite.config.ts` will be clobbered by a future re-scaffold.
- **Do not edit agent-infrastructure dirs** (`.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`).
- **No sibling game repos required:** the game repo's `./core` submodule plus
  `configs/game.json` already select Gym + Main Street.

## Existing state

- Core precedent: `Tableau-Card-Engine/.github/workflows/deploy.yml` runs
  `npm ci`, `npm test`, `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run build`, then
  `actions/configure-pages`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, and
  `actions/deploy-pages@v4`. Its Vite config sets
  `base: mode === 'electron' ? './' : mode === 'production' ? '/Tableau-Card-Engine/' : '/'`.
- `tce-main-street` has **no** `.github/workflows/` directory.
- `tce-main-street/package.json` `build` = `tsc --noEmit && vite build`; `test` =
  `vitest run --project unit`.
- `tce-main-street/vite.config.ts`: `base: mode === 'electron' ? './' : '/'`;
  defaults `GAMES_CONFIG` to `game` (the single-game preset).
- `tce-main-street/.gitmodules`: `core` points at the SSH URL
  `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine.git`.
- Current `dist/index.html` references `/assets/index-*.js` (root-absolute).
- `index.html` page title is the generic "Tableau Card Engine".

## Desired change

- Add `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` to `tce-main-street` (auto on push to
  `main`), mirroring the core workflow: checkout + compose `core` over HTTPS,
  `npm ci`, unit tests, production build, configure/upload/deploy Pages, with a
  `pages` concurrency group and `contents: read`, `pages: write`,
  `id-token: write` permissions.
- Make the **production** Vite base `/tce-main-street/` (done generically — e.g.
  derived from the package/repo name — and reflected in the core scaffold
  template so it survives re-scaffolding).
- Document Pages enablement + release/verification steps in the repo.
- (Small, user-facing) set the page title to a Main Street–specific title.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — **New.** Pages build + deploy workflow
  (auto on `main`, tests → build → deploy).
- `vite.config.ts` — Production `base` becomes `/tce-main-street/` (conditional,
  dev stays `/`).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — Scaffold template for the Vite base so
  the fix is generic and survives re-scaffold. *(cross-repo change to the core
  submodule; follow the core repo's own build → test → commit gates.)*
- `index.html` — Main Street–specific page title (and confirm 404 guard works
  under the new base).
- `README.md` — **New (or first deployment doc).** Pages URL, first-time setup,
  verification steps.
- `RELEASE.md` — **New (optional).** Mirror the core's release/deployment doc for
  the single-game repo.
- `tests/` — Add an automated assertion for the production base path /
  deployed artefact.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUPKEWEC005U2XV` — storyline-author CLI suite timeout (recent release
  hygiene; unrelated but same repo release cadence).
- `MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19` — Visual storyline authoring editor (in-repo web tool;
  shares the "local web tool" concern but different deliverable).
- Upstream: `Tableau-Card-Engine` `CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17` (core/game split) and the
  core Pages deployment (`RELEASE.md`) — the precedent this work mirrors.
- Upstream: `tce-main-street` multi-repo scaffold (`configs/game.json`,
  `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`).

## Verification commands

```bash
# Local reproduction of what CI gates on
npm ci
npm test                 # unit suite (vitest run --project unit)
npm run build            # tsc --noEmit && vite build -> dist/

# Serve the production build and check the Pages base path resolves
npx vite preview --base=/tce-main-street/ --port 4173
# then open http://localhost:4173/tce-main-street/ and confirm the launcher
# loads Main Street with no 404s in the console.
```

## Risks & assumptions

- **Pages must be enabled once by an admin** (Source: GitHub Actions). Until then
  the workflow's deploy step fails — documented as a one-time manual step.
- **Base-path regression risk:** assuming production base changes must not affect
  the Electron build (`'./'`) or dev (`'/'`). Mitigate with the `mode ===
  'production'` conditional, matching the core.
- **Cross-repo scaffold edit:** if `vite.config.ts` is changed without updating
  `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, a future re-scaffold regresses the base.
  The core change must go through the core repo's own work item/gates.
- **Gym appears in the selector** (core-owned, always present). Assumed
  acceptable; the AC scopes "only Main Street" to *example games*.
- **CI test scope:** the repo's `npm test` is unit-only; running the full browser
  suite in the deploy job may be too heavy. Assumption: gate on unit tests +
  build, and add a lightweight post-build smoke check (not a full E2E run).
- **Scope creep:** adding desktop/Steam packaging or per-game Pages for other
  games is out of scope — record as separate work items if raised.
