# Intake Brief: Main Street — Business Payback Rebalance (~5 Turns) and Economy Re-tune

**Work item:** MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 · `task` · `high`

## Headline

Re-derive business `baseIncome` so a business pays for itself in **~5 turns on
average** (cheaper businesses faster, more expensive slower), then re-tune the
compensating balance levers, capture before/after Monte Carlo evidence, and
produce prioritised further-balancing recommendations.

## Problem statement

The cost/income balance makes the game too easy: a business currently recovers
its purchase cost in **~1.3–2.4 turns** (net of its per-turn running cost), so
buildings become profitable almost immediately and runs snowball. On the
canonical harness profile the greedy AI wins 91 % (Easy) / 61.5 % (Medium) /
44 % (Hard) with elevated net liquidity (~6.3 coins/turn on Medium). The
producer wants business payback slowed to a ~5-turn average — with a cost-graded
spread — and the surrounding economy re-tuned so the game stays challenging but
winnable, backed by simulation evidence and concrete follow-up suggestions.

## Users

- **Player** — wants building decisions to carry real economic tension (when to
  buy, which business, how many turns until it pays off) instead of trivial
  snowballing.
  - *"As a player, I want a new business to take several turns to earn back its
    cost, so that choosing when and where to build actually matters."*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants a reproducible, evidence-backed balance
  change with a documented lever set and guardrails.
  - *"As a designer, I want the payback curve to scale with card cost and be
    enforced by tests, so future cards stay in band."*
- **Developer** — wants deterministic contracts, before/after metrics, and an
  auditable baseline update.
  - *"As a developer, I want the payback contract and the regenerated baseline
    to be reproducible from a single commit SHA."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Business payback contract (deterministic, no simulation).** A test over
   `src/card-data.csv` computes net payback per income-generating business as
   `cost ÷ (baseIncome − ongoingCost)` and asserts:
   - (a) the mean net payback across income businesses is **4.5–5.5 turns**;
   - (b) payback is **cost-graded**: cheap businesses pay back faster than
     expensive ones (bucket means strictly increasing by cost band, and/or a
     Spearman rank correlation between cost and payback ≥ 0.6);
   - (c) every income business has positive net income
     (`baseIncome > ongoingCost`);
   - (d) intentional exceptions (0-income reputation cards such as the Clinic,
     producer-overridden costs such as the Charity Shop) are explicitly listed
     with rationale.
2. **Compensating parameters tuned and guardrails hold.** After the income
   change, the canonical 200-seed / 60-turn greedy profile satisfies the
   design-intent bands: win-rate ladder `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard`, and
   `avgCoinsPerTurn` / `medianScore` within their bands — **or** the bands are
   consciously revised with documented rationale per the drift workflow.
   Parameter changes stay within balance levers (business `baseIncome` /
   `ongoingCost`, difficulty presets, and — as needed — community-space, event,
   and upgrade costs).
3. **Monte Carlo evidence captured.** Before/after runs across Easy/Medium/Hard
   (greedy; sweep where useful) are recorded with commit SHAs and summarised in
   the work item **and** `docs/main-street/`. The committed baseline
   (`docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`) is regenerated only via the
   **drift-report-then-ask** workflow in
   `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md` (§0) — never
   silently.
4. **Further-balancing recommendations produced.** A concise artefact (doc or
   work-item comment) presents macro/micro findings (economy health, loss-mode
   decomposition, synergy diversity, outlier/trap cards) and specific,
   prioritised parameter suggestions, each linked to a follow-up work item
   where it is out of scope here.
5. **Documentation updated.** `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md`,
   `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`,
   `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md`, and any affected
   PRD tables reflect the new payback model and values, including code comments.
6. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (`npm test`).

> Standard criteria also met: at least one testing/validation criterion (AC1),
> documentation updated (AC5), and full suite green (AC6). CHANGELOG.md is
> excluded (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Constraints

- **Integer ×100 economy** (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6): `card-data.csv` values are
  integer coin-cent units; payback is computed in whole-coin display units and
  incomes must round to integers.
- **Card-data change is a review trigger** (PRD §3.1) → a structured balance
  review with before/after evidence is mandatory.
- **Lever order** (CG-0MSP26Q5N002EH8P): difficulty presets first; card data for
  card-level outliers. Here card income is the explicit target, so card data
  leads and presets compensate.
- **No engine-rule changes** unless justified and separately tracked (e.g. score
  formula, action economy, synergy formula).
- **Preserve deliberate overrides:** incident cards stay free (cost 0);
  community spaces keep their 0-income reputation/synergy role; the Charity Shop
  keeps its producer-set cost; the Clinic keeps its 0-income reputation design;
  hand-held-business ongoing-cost semantics (CG-0MTC31LN3000UHDY) are unchanged.
- **Baseline discipline:** drift is reported and approved before regeneration.
- **Scope-creep guard:** engine changes, new cards, staff/event re-balancing are
  separate work items; record, don't absorb.

## Existing state

- **Card data:** `src/card-data.csv` — 31 businesses, 8 community spaces.
  Business incomes were last raised by CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE
  (`income = old income + 2.4 × ongoingCost`) with `ongoingCost = max(25, cost/4)`,
  producing the current payback profile.
- **Current measured net payback** (whole coins, `cost ÷ (baseIncome − ongoingCost)`):

  | Card | Cost | Income | Ongoing | Net | Net payback |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | Bakery / Diner / Bookshop / Hardware / Boutique | 3.00 | 2.30 | 0.75 | 1.55 | 1.94 |
  | Pawn Shop | 2.00 | 2.30 | 0.75 | 1.55 | 1.29 |
  | Laundromat / Arcade / Food Truck | 4.00 | 2.90 | 1.00 | 1.90 | 2.11 |
  | Barbershop | 5.00 | 4.00 | 1.25 | 2.75 | 1.82 |
  | Cafe | 7.00 | 5.20 | 1.75 | 3.45 | 2.03 |
  | Art Gallery / Day Spa / Private Clinic | 14.00 | 9.40–10.90 | 3.50 | 5.90–7.40 | 1.89–2.37 |
  | Grand Hotel | 16.00 | 12.10 | 4.00 | 8.10 | 1.98 |
  | Charity Shop | 3.00 | 1.50 | 0.75 | 0.75 | 4.00 |
  | Clinic | 9.00 | 0.00 | 0.50 | −0.50 | n/a (rep card) |

  Average net payback ≈ **2.1 turns** over the 30 income businesses.
- **Difficulty presets** (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`): Easy 1000 start /
  10000 win threshold / 0.5 synergy; Medium 600 / 12000 / 0.35; Hard 400 /
  15000 / 0.25.
- **Monte Carlo harness:** `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` +
  `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts` (`npm run monte-carlo`,
  `npm run monte-carlo-sweep`); baseline generator
  `src/scripts/generate-main-street-monte-baseline.ts`; drift report
  `npm run balance:drift-report`.
- **Balance analysis library:** `src/scripts/balance/` (micro M1–M7, macro
  G1–G8, guardrail thresholds, comparison engine); M3
  `computeCostToIncomeRatio` is the static cost-to-income metric.
- **Guardrail tests:** `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts`
  (design intent), `monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` (baseline drift),
  `monte-carlo-balance.test.ts` (smoke).
- **Committed baseline** (`docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`,
  200 seeds / 60 turns): greedy win rate Easy 0.91 / Medium 0.615 / Hard 0.44;
  Medium net liquidity 632.99 (×100 units) and median score 12332.5 (×100).
- **Balancing algorithm/docs:** `src/balance-cards/`,
  `src/scripts/run-balance-cards.ts` (`npm run balance-cards`),
  `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md`.

## Desired change

1. **Derive incomes from a payback target.** Set
   `baseIncome = cost ÷ targetPayback + ongoingCost`, with `targetPayback`
   rising with cost so the **mean across income businesses is ~5 turns** — e.g.
   ~3–4 turns for cost-2–4 cards, ~5 turns for mid-cost (7–10), ~6.5–7 turns
   for cost-14–16 flagships. Round to integer cent units.
2. **Re-tune compensating levers** so the tighter economy stays winnable and
   paced: adjust difficulty presets (starting coins / win thresholds / synergy),
   and review `ongoingCost` and community-space / event / upgrade pricing where
   the payback model breaks down. Document every change and its rationale.
3. **Measure.** Re-run the Monte Carlo harness for each difficulty before and
   after; record metrics and commit SHAs; regenerate the baseline via the drift
   workflow only after review.
4. **Recommend.** Produce further-balancing suggestions from the macro/micro
   reports (e.g. community spaces, events, upgrades, difficulty bands), each
   linked to a follow-up work item.
5. **Enforce.** Add the deterministic payback contract so future card additions
   cannot silently drift out of band.

### Candidate payback targets (illustrative — to be finalised during planning)

| Cost band | Example cards | Target net payback |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2–4 | Pawn Shop, Bakery, Laundromat, Arcade | ~3.5 |
| 5–7 | Barbershop, Cafe, Flower Shop, Teahouse | ~5.0 |
| 8–10 | Yoga Studio, Gym, Physiotherapist, Clinic* | ~5.5 |
| 12–16 | Dentist, Art Gallery, Day Spa, Grand Hotel | ~6.5–7.0 |

\* Clinic has no income by design; excluded from the mean, handled as a
documented exception.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — Re-derive business `baseIncome` (and review
  `ongoingCost`) for the ~5-turn payback target; integer cent units.
- `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — Compensating preset tuning
  (`startingCoins`, `winThreshold`, `synergyBonusPerNeighbor`, incident knobs).
- `tests/main-street/business-payback.test.ts` (new) — Deterministic payback
  contract: mean ≈5, cost-graded monotone, positive net income, documented
  exceptions.
- `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/clinic-health-synergy.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/charity-shop.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/group-a-*`/`expanded-card-pool*`,
  `tests/main-street/community-space-*.test.ts` — Update assertions pinned to
  old income values.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-balance.test.ts` — Guardrail bands / baseline
  assertions after re-tune.
- `src/scripts/balance/guards/thresholds.ts` — Threshold band updates if the
  review revises them.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/card-metrics.ts` — Extend M3 (or add a companion)
  to report **net** payback (`cost ÷ (baseIncome − ongoingCost)`), not just
  gross cost/income.
- `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json` — Regenerated baseline (drift
  workflow; commit-stamped).
- `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts`,
  `src/scripts/generate-main-street-monte-baseline.ts`,
  `src/scripts/balance/drift-report.ts` — Generate before/after evidence.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — Document the payback model and
  revised per-family strategy.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — Refresh card stat tables.
- `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md` — Record measured
  after-state and any band revisions.
- `src/scripts/run-balance-cards.ts` / `src/balance-cards/` — Ensure the reward
  spread respects the payback target if the balancing pass is re-run.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE** — Business ongoing costs + income raise
  (`income = old + 2.4 × ongoingCost`); the economy this item re-tunes.
- **CG-0MTC31LN3000UHDY** — Hand-held businesses no longer incur ongoing costs;
  the semantics the payback model must respect.
- **CG-0MSP26Q5N002EH8P** — Economy re-tune and the "presets first" lever order.
- **CG-0MSRKN325004ELH2** — Guardrail band recommendations.
- **CG-0MUE03DGQ005KPZ7** — Drift attribution workflow; baseline commit stamping.
- **CG-0MTH5CC4H003Q4B3** — Investment events cost one action (economy
  interaction to watch).
- **CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6** — Integer ×100 economy.
- **MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL** — Charity Shop manual cost override.
- **MS-0MUMC6IVF0098WRL** — Per-turn running costs for community spaces.
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** — Staff cost-reduction effects (interacts with
  effective cost/payback).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Payback definition (assumption).** Net payback = `cost ÷ (baseIncome −
  ongoingCost)` in whole coins, excluding synergy/event income. "Profit" is read
  as revenue minus running cost. Gross `cost ÷ baseIncome` is also reported.
  *Producer confirmation requested (see Appendix Q1).*
- **Magnitude.** Reaching ~5 turns means roughly a **2.4× income cut** (or
  equivalent), which will materially tighten the economy: expect lower liquidity,
  slower score growth, and more bankruptcies. Compensating levers must be tuned
  together, not income alone.
- **Synergy distortion.** Low base incomes make synergy/`{SYNERGY_RATE}` a larger
  share of a business's income, potentially making placement dominate base
  economy. Monitor synergy utilisation and diversity in the macro report.
- **Community spaces, events, upgrades.** These carry no business payback; if
  their pricing is left untouched they may become relatively over/under-valued.
  Review is in scope for AC2/AC4 but changes are evidence-led.
- **Guardrail churn.** A large intentional balance change will breach
  baseline-relative drift. Follow the drift-report-then-ask workflow and do not
  silently regenerate.
- **Scope-creep risk.** New cards, staff re-balancing, and engine-rule changes
  are out of scope; record as linked follow-up work items (AC4).
- **Determinism.** The payback contract must be fully deterministic (CSV-only),
  independent of simulation seeds.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

All entries below are research-driven and are recorded for producer
confirmation; the recommended interpretation was used to draft this brief.

- **Q1 (payback definition):** *Should the 5-turn payback be measured net of the
  business's per-turn running cost (`cost ÷ (baseIncome − ongoingCost)`) or
  gross (`cost ÷ baseIncome`)?*
  **Answer (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** Net of running cost —
  "turns to profit" is read as recovering the purchase cost after operating
  costs, which is the game's actual economic break-even. Gross payback will also
  be reported for transparency. Research: `ongoingCost = max(25, cost/4)` is
  deducted every turn (`applyBusinessOngoingCosts`, business-ongoing-cost
  tests); M3 currently models only gross `cost/baseIncome`, so a net companion
  is proposed. Source: `src/card-data.csv`, `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`,
  `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md`.
- **Q2 (average weighting & spread):** *Is the "average of 5 turns" a simple
  mean across income businesses, and how should it vary with cost?*
  **Answer (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** A simple mean of ~5
  turns across income-generating businesses, with a cost-graded spread (cheap
  ≈3.5, mid ≈5, flagship ≈6.5–7), exactly as the operator described ("more
  expensive … longer … cheaper … quicker"). Clinic (0 income) and Charity Shop
  (manual override) are documented exceptions. Source: operator request; current
  payback table (this brief).
- **Q3 (compensating levers):** *Which parameters may be adjusted to keep the
  game winnable?*
  **Answer (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** Balance levers only —
  difficulty presets, business `ongoingCost`, and community-space/event/upgrade
  pricing as needed. Engine rules (score formula, action economy) are out of
  scope and would be raised as separate work items. Research: the "presets
  first, card data for outliers" lever order in
  `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md` §4. Source: repo docs.
- **Q4 (guardrail bands):** *If the tighter economy moves guardrail metrics
  outside the current bands, revise bands or keep tuning?*
  **Answer (recommended, pending producer confirmation):** Tune the compensating
  levers first; revise a band only if the measured outcome is genuinely the
  intended design, with written rationale per the drift workflow. Source:
  `docs/main-street/balance-guardrail-recommendations.md` §0.

**Parent:** MS-0MUQ1KXAS003FJ42 · `feature`

**Parent ACs covered:** 1 (auto-deploy on ship), 2 (Main Street only, with launcher), 4 (gated deployment), 5 (no stored SSH credentials), 9 (full project test suite passes).

**Goal.** Add `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` so every push to `main` runs the
quality gates and publishes `dist/` to GitHub Pages at
`https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/`.

**Reuse.** Mirror `core/.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (same action versions,
`pages` concurrency group, `github-pages` environment, three-step configure /
upload / deploy) but drop the sibling-game composition step: this repo's
`./configs/game.json` preset already selects the core-owned Gym plus Main Street.

**Test-first.** The workflow contract test is written before the workflow file and
committed with it, so this item lands green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **1.** Auto-deploy on ship: every push to `main` runs a GitHub Actions workflow that builds `tce-main-street` and deploys `dist/` to GitHub Pages at `https://thewizardscode.github.io/tce-main-street/`.
- **2.** Gated deployment: the workflow runs unit tests and the production build first, and a failing test or build blocks deployment so no artefact is published.
- **3.** No stored SSH credentials: the build composes the `./core` submodule from the public core repo over HTTPS, needing no SSH secrets or `ssh-key` input.
- **4.** Main Street only (with launcher): the published site shows the launcher with exactly one playable example game, Main Street.
- **5.** The build uses the single-game preset and never `GAMES_CONFIG=full`, and no sibling `tce-<game>` repository is cloned, so no other example game can appear in the selector; the core-owned Gym is always present.
- **6.** Steps are ordered install (`npm ci`) → test (`npm test`) → build (`npm run build`) → `actions/configure-pages@v5` → `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3` (`path: dist`) → `actions/deploy-pages@v4`, and no other trigger can publish unreleased work.
- **7.** `permissions` are exactly `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`; `concurrency` is `group: pages` with `cancel-in-progress: true`; the job uses `environment: github-pages` and exposes the deployed `page_url`.
- **8.** `tests/deploy/deploy-workflow.test.ts` parses the workflow YAML and asserts the trigger, step order, permissions, concurrency, the absence of secret/SSH references, and the absence of `GAMES_CONFIG=full`; the test fails if any of those are removed.
- **9.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes: `npm test` is green.

- Add `tests/deploy/deploy-workflow.test.ts` first (adapted from `core/tests/scripts/deploy-workflow.test.ts`).

**Dependencies:** `Pages base-path build tests`, `Production Pages build correctness`.

# Re-price community spaces and events relative to the slower business payback

## Problem statement

With businesses now taking ~5 turns to pay back (mean 4.87, median 5.00), community spaces and investment events have shifted in relative value. Community spaces — which provide reputation but no coin income — may be over-valued relative to businesses; investment events show wide ROI spread (0.36x–1.50x) and some are materially over-priced. This work item reviews both and applies evidence-led price changes.

## Users

- **Producer / balance owner** — wants a balanced economy where community spaces serve their intended role (reputation provision) without being dominant, and events offer fair value.
- **Players** — experience meaningful choices between business investment, community space placement, and event spending.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **ROI comparison.** A quantitative comparison of community-space and investment-event ROI against the business payback profile (mean 4.87 turns) is documented, including synergy-income analysis for community spaces and one-shot ROI for events.
2. **Evidence-led price changes.** Community-space and event rows in `src/card-data.csv` are adjusted where the comparison shows material imbalance, or changes are documented with rationale where no change is warranted.
3. **Canonical profile preserved.** After changes, the 200-seed / 60-turn greedy profile satisfies the design-intent guardrails: win-rate ladder `Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard` holds, `avgCoinsPerTurn` / `medianScore` within bands, and no regression in balance.

## Constraints

- **Balance levers only.** Changes limited to `card-data.csv` cost / `ongoingCost` / `reputationPerTurn` / event coinDelta / reputationDelta for community spaces and events. No engine-rule changes.
- **Integer economy.** All coin values are whole integers.
- **Data is source of truth.** Tooltip, overlay, and deduction derive from CSV values.
- **Ladder preserved.** Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard is the primary gate.
- **Synergy anchors.** Community space synergy contribution to neighbours must be preserved.

## Existing state

### Business payback (post-rebalance, mean 4.87 turns)

| Cost band | Examples | Payback |
|---|---|---|
| Cheap (200–400) | Bakery, Diner, Pawn Shop, Arcade | ~3.5 turns |
| Mid (500–800) | Barbershop, Cinema, Pharmacy, Gym | ~5.0–5.5 turns |
| Flagship (1000–1600) | Dentist, Private Clinic, Art Gallery, Grand Hotel | ~6.5–7.0 turns |

### Community spaces (baseIncome = 0, no coin synergy income)

| Space | Cost | Ongoing/turn | Rep/turn |
|---|---|---|---|
| Park | 300 | 40 | 0 |
| Library | 700 | 25 | 10 |
| Playground | 400 | 0 | 5 |
| Community Garden | 500 | 10 | 10 |
| Town Fountain | 500 | 0 | 10 |
| Health Kiosk | 600 | 15 | 15 |
| Community Shelter | 600 | 0 | 15 |
| Public Art | 800 | 25 | 20 |

### Investment events (ROI per coin spent)

| ROI tier | Events | ROI |
|---|---|---|
| High (≥1.4x) | Grand Opening Sale, Charity Drive, Volunteer Day | 1.50x |
| Good (1.0–1.4x) | Block Party, Bulk Purchase, Book Fair, Harvest Festival, St Patrick's Day, Christmas | 1.0–1.4x |
| Moderate (0.7–1.0x) | Local Festival, Wellness Fair, Garden Party, May Day, Lughnasadh, Samhain, Easter, St Brigid's Day | 0.6–1.0x |
| Low (<0.7x) | Shopping Spree, Summer Fest, Service Week, Health Carnival, Food Tasting Tour, Art Sale | 0.36–0.60x |

### Supporting evidence

- Reputation collapse is the dominant loss mode on Medium (69% of losses), making reputation-providing community spaces strategically valuable.
- Net liquidity is 2–4 coins/turn on every difficulty — the game ends earlier (~10–12 turns), not poorer.
- Upgrades appear in ≤1% of runs (separate work item MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M addresses this).
- Three community spaces (Playground, Town Fountain, Community Shelter) currently have 0 ongoing cost; retiering with running costs is tracked under MS-0MUMC6IVF0098WRL.

## Key Files

- `src/card-data.csv` — community-space and event rows
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts` — guardrail assertions
- `src/scripts/balance/guards/thresholds.ts` — guardrail band values
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — methodology documentation
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — card value documentation

## Related work

- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3** — Parent: Five-turn business payback rebalance (completed).
- **MS-0MUQUBKNE007NYR8** — Further-balancing recommendations (source of R4).
- **MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M** — Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI (R1, related).
- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** — Re-tune reputation sources (R2, related).
- **MS-0MUMC6IVF0098WRL** — Add per-turn running costs to Playground, Town Fountain, Community Shelter (related, intake_complete).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** Community spaces earn zero synergy coin income (baseIncome = 0). Their value is reputation only + role as synergy anchors for neighbours. Verified against `MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` formula: `synergy = effectiveBase × synergyCoinBonus × bonusPerNeighbor × N`, where effectiveBase = (baseIncome + incomeBonus) × sameTypePenalty = 0 for community spaces.
- **Assumption:** Community Favour conversion (200 rep → 300 coins, i.e. 1 rep = 1.5 coins) provides a reasonable coin-equivalent for reputation. The coins-to-rep direction (200 coins → 1 rep) is lossy and not used as a conversion path.
- **Risk:** Event ROI analysis assumes one-shot resolution (no duration/multiplier effects). Events with `duration > 0` and `effectType` (e.g. income-multiplier events like Tourist Season, Community Renovation) have implicit value from sustained effects that simple ROI doesn't capture.
- **Risk:** Price changes to events may shift their availability tier or trigger distribution. Re-run Monte Carlo to verify no unintended cascade.
- **Scope creep:** Business pricing, upgrade costs, and difficulty preset tuning are out of scope. These are tracked under separate work items (R1–R3).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** What is the target relationship between community space value and business payback? — **Answer (research):** Community spaces should not be dominant compared to businesses. At 5-turn payback, a community space's effective coin-equivalent value (rep × 1.5 + synergy-anchor value) should not exceed the opportunity cost of a 3.5–5.0 turn business investment. Research: computed synergy income (0 for baseIncome=0 spaces), reputation-to-coin conversion (1.5:1), and Monte Carlo loss-mode data (69% reputation-collapse on Medium).
- **Q:** Should events with duration/multiplier effects (e.g. Tourist Season, Flu Outbreak) be excluded from ROI analysis? — **Answer:** Yes — these events provide sustained effects over multiple turns, and their value is better assessed via Monte Carlo than simple one-shot ROI. Source: seed context + `card-data.csv` analysis.
- **Q:** Are the three retiered community spaces (Playground, Fountain, Shelter) in scope for this intake, or for MS-0MUMC6IVF0098WRL? — **Answer (agent recommendation):** Include them — their final pricing must account for both the new running cost and the 5-turn payback context. MS-0MUMC6IVF0098WRL handles the running-cost mechanism; this intake handles the price calibration. Source: intake analysis.

# Activity Log Should Not Show Log Lines Until Results Are Displayed in UI

## Problem Statement

During the end-of-turn cycle, activity log entries are rendered in the UI before the corresponding UI results (e.g. upcoming cards, phase transitions) have been displayed. This gives the player a misleading sequence of events — for example, log lines about upcoming cards appear before the upcoming cards are actually shown on screen.

## Users

- **Player**: Observes the activity log alongside the main game UI; expects log entries to be displayed in chronological order with the visual events they describe.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Log entries added during `processEndOfTurn()` must not be rendered in the activity log panel until after the upcoming/phase UI updates have been displayed to the player.
2. The fix must not affect the content of log entries — only their timing of appearance.
3. Reduced-motion mode must continue to work correctly (log entries should still appear in the correct order, even if animations are skipped).
4. Tutorial mode must not be affected — the existing tutorial pacing must remain unchanged.
5. All existing activity log tests must continue to pass.
6. New tests verify the render-deferral timing for the deferred-mutation end-of-turn path.

## Constraints

- The fix must be minimal and surgical — only defer log rendering, do not change log entry content or order.
- Must preserve the deferred-mutation HUD window pattern (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q).
- Must not affect replay mode or headless mode.

## Existing State

- Log entries are pushed to `state.activityLog` during `processEndOfTurn()` in `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`.
- `refreshLog()` in `MainStreetRendererHud.ts` renders entries when `activityLog.length` changes (tracked via `logPrevEntryCount`).
- `refreshLog()` is called in `finishTurnPresentation()` which runs **before** `startTurnPhase()` (where upcoming cards are displayed).
- The deferred-mutation path (`requiresDeferredClosing === true`) calls `refreshAll()` in `finalizeTurn()` after the closing animations, but still before `startTurnPhase()`.

## Desired Change

Defer the first render of new log entries until after the upcoming/phase UI updates have been displayed. This can be achieved by:

1. Adding a flag (e.g. `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`) that prevents `refreshLog()` from rendering new entries during the initial post-turn-refresh.
2. Clearing the flag at the appropriate point in the flow (after `startTurnPhase()` has displayed upcoming cards).
3. At that point, triggering a log refresh to render all accumulated entries.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — `refreshLog()` function needs modification to support deferred rendering
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `finishTurnPresentation()` / `finalizeTurn()` / `startTurnPhase()` — need to coordinate log render deferral
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — may need a new method or flag on the context
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — may need a new field to track log render state
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — read-only reference for understanding where log entries are added

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: The fix is narrowly scoped to log rendering timing only; do not defer other UI updates.
- **Assumption**: The fix should use a simple boolean flag (`logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`) rather than a more complex event system.
- **Risk**: If the log render is deferred too long, the player might not see log entries at all during very short turns; ensure the log still renders when the next turn's log entries are added.
- **Risk**: Browser tests that rely on log entry timing may need updates to account for the new deferral.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What specific log lines appear too early?" — Answer (operator): "Log lines such as 'upcoming cards' appear in the log before the upcoming phase of the end turn cycle has completed." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Does this affect all modes (normal, reduced-motion, tutorial)?" — Answer: Not specified; assume it affects normal mode primarily but should be verified for all modes. Source: assumption (marked for verification).

## Related Work

- CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q: Deferred HUD window — the existing pattern for deferring HUD updates during animations.
- CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I: Incident reveal presentation — similar deferred presentation pattern.
- MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9: Storyline options (no direct relevance).
- MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0: Staff action points (no direct relevance).

# Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want to play against one or more AI opponents from the game UI, so that I can enjoy a competitive mode without needing a second human player.

This epic covers the three enabling steps required to make **AI competitive mode playable**:

1. Plan the UI/scene work (design the competitive-mode rendering, input, turn orchestration and overlay changes).
2. Add a game-mode selector (Single-player vs Competitive, with opponent count and per-AI strategy/difficulty).
3. Wire up the AI player so `MainStreetAiPlayer` drives AI turns against the engine's competitive turn orchestrator, interleaved with human turns.

## Background

- The engine-level competitive mode (shared day, per-player wallets/ownership, N-player-ready, `competitiveWinnerId`) shipped as a deliberate scope extension (`CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`) in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` and `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`.
- Milestone 3 explicitly deferred the UI: "AI vs. player (competitive mode) | **Superseded** — engine-level competitive mode shipped …; rendering/scene deferred to a planning child" (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md`).
- Three selectable AI strategies already exist in `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `Random`, `Greedy`, `BankingGreedy` — plus the `MainStreetAiPlayer` wrapper and `enumerateLegalActions`/`executeAction` seams. They are currently used headlessly only (Monte Carlo balance harness, hint generation, auto-play).
- Game setup currently presents a single-player flow only (`configs/game.json` selects one game; `MainStreetScene` has no mode selector).

## Scope

### 1. Plan the UI/scene work
Produce a design/plan (via `/skill:plan`) for competitive-mode scene changes: player roster/score display, per-player turn indication, action routing between human and AI seats, overlay/HUD changes, and persistence/save-load across multiple players.

### 2. Add a game-mode selector
Let the player choose **Single-player** vs **Competitive (human vs AI)** at game start, including:
- number of AI opponents (>= 1);
- per-opponent AI strategy (Random / Greedy / BankingGreedy) and difficulty (Easy / Medium / Hard);
- propagate the selection into the competitive state created by the engine.

### 3. Wire up the AI player
Drive `MainStreetAiPlayer` to consume engine actions on each AI player's turn under the shared-day competitive turn orchestrator, returning control to the human player between seats, with no manual intervention and no stalls.

## Out of scope

- Spectator/replay visuals for AI-vs-AI matches — tracked as a separate work item (discovered-from this epic).
- Networked or local multi-human play; competitive mode is human vs AI only for this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Competitive game can be started from the UI.** The player can start a new game in Competitive mode, choosing at least one AI opponent and each AI's strategy/difficulty, and the selection is reflected in the created game state. *Metric: manual playthrough plus a test asserting the state's `players[]` and per-player strategy/difficulty match the selection.*
2. **AI turns are driven end-to-end.** Each AI seat's actions are chosen by `MainStreetAiPlayer` and applied through the competitive engine path with no manual intervention. *Metric: an automated integration test plays a full competitive game to a terminal condition.*
3. **Human and AI share the competitive path.** The human player's actions are routed through the same competitive engine path as the AI (shared day), and per-player coins/reputation/score are correct for every player. *Metric: integration test asserts per-player state divergence; UI displays each player's wallet and score.*
4. **Games resolve without deadlock.** A full competitive game completes and resolves a winner via the engine end conditions (`competitiveWinnerId` / score / bankruptcy / reputation collapse). *Metric: test plays multiple seeds to completion with no timeouts or stalls.*
5. **Single-player is unchanged.** Single-player mode has no behavioural or balance regression. *Metric: existing single-player unit/integration tests pass and Monte Carlo baselines are unchanged.*

## Dependencies and notes

- Child items will be created under this epic by the plan phase; the design/plan item (scope 1) blocks the selector and AI-wiring children.
- Reuse the engine AI seams (`enumerateLegalActions`, `scoreAction`, `executeAction`) rather than duplicating game logic.
- Keep save/load working for competitive states (`src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`).

# Reject illegal moves before animation and action-point deduction

> **Headline:** A move that cannot be completed must be rejected by a non-mutating legality check before any animation starts or any action/coin is spent; on rejection the player gets illegal-move feedback and keeps their selection to try a different move.

## Problem statement

When the player attempts a move that cannot be completed — most obviously placing a business from hand with too few coins — the UI starts the card-transfer animation and the action point is deducted before the failure is discovered. The player loses a weekly action and sees a transfer that never actually lands. Legality should be established **before** any animation, phase change, or state mutation; an illegal attempt should give feedback and leave the game exactly as it was so the player can choose another move.

## Users

- **Main Street player (MarketPhase)** — "As a player, when I click a slot I cannot legally place on, I want to be told immediately and lose nothing, so I can pick a different slot or a different move without wasting my week's action."
- **Main Street player (held card)** — "As a player holding a card from a previous week, if I no longer have enough coins, I want the illegal-move feedback rather than a phantom animation and a spent action."
- **Main Street player (upgrades)** — "As a player applying an upgrade I cannot afford, I want the same no-cost rejection and to keep the upgrade selected so I can retarget."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Placing a hand business on an empty slot with insufficient coins performs **no** card-transfer animation, leaves `actionsRemaining`, `bankedActions`, `resourceBank.coins`, the hand contents, `uiPhase` and the selected hand card **unchanged**, and plays the standard illegal-move feedback (`playIllegalFeedback` — ILLEGAL_MOVE SFX + shake) with a clear instruction message (e.g. "Not enough coins… need X, have Y").
2. Applying an upgrade from hand with insufficient coins (or an otherwise illegal target) likewise leaves the action budget, coins, hand, target business and pending selection unchanged, and shows illegal feedback **without** starting the transfer animation.
3. The invariant holds for **every action-consuming UI move path** (place-business-from-hand, apply-upgrade-from-hand, buy-and-place drag for business/upgrade, move-to-hand for business/upgrade/event, buy/play event, hire-staff, peek, community-favour, close-business, end-turn): legality is checked with a non-mutating predicate **before** any mutation, and action consumption is atomic with a successful operation (a failed command must not consume an action). The command layer reaches parity with the engine `executeAction` path, which already restores the action on failure.
4. After an illegal attempt the player can immediately try another legal target or move (selection retained), and no path leaves the scene stuck in `uiPhase === 'animating'`.
5. Automated regression tests cover the not-enough-coins placement and upgrade cases at the controller/command level, asserting that no action/coins/hand change and no transfer animation starts; the command layer's restore-on-throw behaviour is covered by extending the existing action-restore suite.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing same-week composite pricing (CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN): the +50% premium replaces the missing action, and the premium explainer dialog ordering must not regress.
- Preserve undo/redo correctness: action/coin/state snapshots must still restore exactly (the undo manager snapshots on first `do()`).
- No new gameplay rules — this is a timing/atomicity fix only; move legality rules themselves are unchanged.
- Keep existing legal-move behaviour and feedback messages intact; reuse `playIllegalFeedback` and the current instruction-text conventions.
- Follow the repo's existing controller/command split; no engine rule changes beyond adding/using non-mutating legality predicates.

## Existing state

- `MainStreetTurnControllerPlaceSell.ts` → `onSlotClick()` (place-from-hand branch): clears `pendingHandIndex`, sets `uiPhase = 'animating'`, and calls `animateTransferFromMarket(...)` **before** any legality check. The placement command runs in `afterTransfer()`. Only the premium sub-branch pre-gates affordability (`coins < premiumCost`); the held-card / listed-cost branch has no pre-gate.
- `MainStreetCommands.ts` → `playBusinessFromHandCommand()` calls `consumeAction(s)` **then** `playBusinessFromHand(...)`; `playBusinessFromHand()` throws `Not enough coins…` before mutating. `snapshotAction`'s `do()` has no try/catch restore, and `UndoRedoManager.execute()` pushes the command only after `do()` succeeds — so the spent action persists after the throw.
- Same pattern for `playUpgradeFromHandCommand()` → `consumeAction()` then `playUpgradeFromHand()` (throws `Not enough coins…`).
- The engine path `executeAction()` **does** restore actions on failure (covered by `tests/main-street/action-restore-on-failure.test.ts`) — the gap is the UI/command path used by click and drag handlers.
- Non-mutating predicates already exist and should be reused: `canPlaceFromHand` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`), `canSellBusiness`, `canPurchaseBusiness`, `canPurchaseEvent`, `canPurchaseStaff`, `canBuyAndPlaceUpgrade`, `isEligibleUpgradeTarget`.

## Desired change

1. In `onSlotClick` (place-from-hand) and `applyHandUpgradeToSlot`, run the non-mutating legality predicate (occupancy, affordability against the applicable listed/premium cost, upgrade target eligibility, tutorial gating) **before** clearing the selection, changing `uiPhase`, or starting `animateTransferFromMarket`. On failure: call `playIllegalFeedback`, set the instruction text, **keep the selection**, and return.
2. Make action consumption atomic in the command layer: either consume the action only after the underlying operation succeeds, or have the snapshot action restore its pre-snapshot when `do()` throws. This removes the class of bug for any future callers.
3. Audit every action-consuming handler enumerated in AC3 for the same "animate/consume before validate" ordering and fix any other offenders found.

- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — atomic action consumption / restore-on-throw for the `*Command` factories (`playBusinessFromHandCommand`, `playUpgradeFromHandCommand`, `buyAndPlaceBusinessCommand`, `buyAndPlaceUpgradeCommand`, `moveToHandCommand`, `moveEventToHandCommand`, `hireStaffCardCommand`, `closeBusinessCommand`).

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerUtils.ts` — `playIllegalFeedback` (reuse; no change expected).
- `tests/main-street/action-restore-on-failure.test.ts` — extend to cover the command layer's restore-on-throw.
- `tests/main-street/click-place.browser.test.ts` — browser regression: illegal placement does not animate, does not spend an action, and keeps the card selected/playable.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetPlaceSell.test.ts` — controller-level legality/affordability assertions.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — document that transfer animations only start for legal moves and that illegal feedback precedes any mutation.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — clarify the "legality before action spend" invariant in the action-economy notes.

## Related work

- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — card transfer feedback, illegal feedback, and commit-before-feedback conventions.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — action economy and same-week composite pricing (CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN).

## Command Layer: Atomic Action Consumption on Failure (AC2)

**Goal:** Make action consumption atomic in the command layer so failed commands never lose an action.

**Problem:** snapshotAction.do() in MainStreetCommands.ts calls consumeAction(state) before the actual operation. If the operation throws after consuming, the snapshot was captured but the command is never pushed to the undo stack (UndoRedoManager.execute only pushes after do() succeeds). The action is lost.

**Fix:** Wrap the do() body in a try/catch — if an error is thrown, restore the pre-snapshot action budget (actionsRemaining, bankedActions) before re-throwing. This gives any caller (UI handlers, engine, etc.) the same restore-on-failure semantics as the engine's executeAction path.

**Key file:** src/MainStreetCommands.ts — snapshotAction() function

## Acceptance Criteria

- snapshotAction.do() catches any throw from doFn and restores actionsRemaining and bankedActions to their pre-snapshot values before re-throwing.
- Executing playBusinessFromHandCommand and playUpgradeFromHandCommand with insufficient coins via UndoRedoManager throws and leaves actionsRemaining, bankedActions, resourceBank.coins and hand contents unchanged.
- On successful execution the action is consumed exactly once (no double-decrement) and undo restores it exactly.
- No behaviour change for non-action or already-safe commands (refreshMarket, sellBusiness, discardFromHand, resolveEventChoice, etc.).
- Extended tests in tests/main-street/action-restore-on-failure.test.ts cover the command-layer restore-on-throw path and pass.

# Problem Statement

In competitive (human vs AI) mode, when the human player ends their turn and AI opponents complete their shared-day sequence, the closing phases (Income → Incident → EndCheck) run silently in the engine — the player receives no feedback about what happened. The only message shown is "AI opponents are taking their turns..." before the next day begins immediately.

# Users

- **Competitive mode players**: Human players facing AI opponents want to understand the outcome of each shared day — what income was earned, whether incidents occurred, and whether challenges were completed.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **Income Phase feedback**: After AI opponents complete their turns and the shared closing Income phase runs, the player sees a brief income summary (total coins earned) and/or income phase labels, matching the visual feedback shown in single-player.
2. **Incident Phase feedback**: If an incident is resolved during the closing phase, the player sees the incident reveal animation and its name (matching the single-player incident reveal).
3. **End Check feedback**: The instruction text reflects the closing phase progression (e.g., "Resolving end-of-turn effects..." or "End of turn complete") between the AI actions and the next day start.
4. **No stalling or blocking**: The closing presentation must be non-blocking and bounded — the next day must always start within a reasonable time, even if animations are skipped (reduced motion, replay mode).
5. **Single-player unchanged**: The single-player end-turn flow and presentation must be byte-for-byte unchanged.

# Constraints

- The fix must work in both the Phaser scene context (with animations) and headless/replay contexts (no animations).
- Must respect the existing `reducedMotion` setting — animations should be skipped but text feedback should still appear.
- Must not introduce blocking delays that could stall the game loop.
- The `endCompetitiveTurnDay` function must remain the single entry point for ending a competitive day from the scene.

# Existing State

In `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`, `endCompetitiveTurnDay`:
1. Sets instruction text to "AI opponents are taking their turns..."
2. Calls `driveAiSeatsUntilClosing` — drives each AI seat through their MarketPhase
3. Calls `runCompetitiveClosing` — resolves Income → Incident → EndCheck (returns a `TurnResult`)
4. If the game continues, immediately calls `startTurnPhase()` — **no presentation of the closing phases**

In contrast, the single-player path in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `endTurn`:
1. Calls `processEndOfTurn` (with deferred mode support)
2. Runs `animateIncomePhases` with phase labels
3. Calls `finishTurnPresentation` which shows income/incident text, incident reveal animation, challenge celebration VFX
4. Then calls `startTurnPhase()`

# Desired Change

After `runCompetitiveClosing` returns in `endCompetitiveTurnDay`, present the closing phase results to the player using a similar flow to the single-player path (adapted for the non-interactive AI phase):

- Show income summary (total coins + optional phase breakdown)
- Show incident reveal (if incident occurred)
- Briefly show "End of turn complete" or similar before advancing to the next day

The presentation should be condensed (shorter hold times than single-player, since the player didn't participate in the AI actions) but still provide meaningful feedback.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — `endCompetitiveTurnDay` needs to present closing results after `runCompetitiveClosing`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `animateIncomePhases` / `showIncomePhaseLabel` for income feedback

# Action Banking is Broken in Competitive (Human vs AI) Mode

## Problem Statement

When playing competitive mode (human vs AI opponent(s)), unused actions at the end of the shared day are not banked correctly — the `state.bankedActions` value is lost because `bindCompetitiveSeat` overwrites `state.actionsRemaining` with the player's `actionBudget` without preserving the shared `state.bankedActions` value. This means the human player never gets the benefit of banking actions across turns when playing against AI.

## Users

- **Competitive mode players** who want to bank unused actions across turns, as they can in single-player mode.

### User Story

> As a competitive-mode player, I want to bank unused actions at the end of each shared day so that I can carry them forward to subsequent days — matching the single-player behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Banked actions persist across days in competitive mode.** If a shared day ends with 0 or 1 unused actions, exactly 1 action is banked (up to the cap of 2), regardless of how many seats (human + AI) acted during the day.
2. **Banked actions are correctly consumed by subsequent seats.** When `bindCompetitiveSeat` is called for a seat (human or AI), `state.actionsRemaining` reflects the player's action budget PLUS any currently banked actions — ensuring the bank is not double-consumed or silently lost.
3. **Single-player mode is unchanged.** The fix only affects competitive seat binding; single-player turn flow must remain byte-for-byte identical.
4. **All existing tests pass.** Including competitive-scene-turn-flow, main-street engine tests, and browser integration tests.
5. **Banked actions appear correctly in the HUD.** The banked count display (`state.bankedActions`) remains accurate throughout the competitive day.

## Constraints

- The fix must not change the `consumeAction` contract (which decrements both `state.actionsRemaining` and `state.bankedActions`).
- The per-player `actionBudget` field must remain as the player's daily base budget (without banked actions), consistent with its role in `executeCompetitiveWeekStart`.
- The shared `state.bankedActions` field represents the collective banked actions pool and must be correctly accounted for at every seat transition.

## Existing State

In competitive mode, the shared-day flow works as follows:

1. `executeCompetitiveWeekStart` sets each player's `actionBudget = 1 + staffBonus + min(2, state.bankedActions)`.
2. For each seat (human then AI): `bindCompetitiveSeat` → actions → `restoreCompetitiveSeat`.
3. After all seats act, `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` runs the closing tail, which banks unused actions: `state.bankedActions = min(2, state.bankedActions + min(state.actionsRemaining, 1))`.

**The bug:** `bindCompetitiveSeat` (line 2020 of `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`) sets:
```typescript
state.actionsRemaining = player.actionBudget;
```
This does **not** include `state.bankedActions`. When the human acts first and uses actions (including banked ones via `consumeAction`), `state.bankedActions` is decremented. When the next seat binds, the new `state.actionsRemaining = player.actionBudget` does not account for the (now-depleted) banked actions, effectively losing the bank.

## Desired Change

Update `bindCompetitiveSeat` to include banked actions in the shared `state.actionsRemaining`:

```typescript
state.actionsRemaining = player.actionBudget + state.bankedActions;
```

This ensures each seat's action budget is the sum of their base budget AND any banked actions carried forward.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `bindCompetitiveSeat` (line ~2020) — **needs fix**
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `finishCompetitiveClosingTail` (banking logic) — correct
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — `consumeAction` (line ~333) — correct, no change needed
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — seat driver — no change needed
- `tests/main-street/competitive-scene-turn-flow.test.ts` — add banking test
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `bankedActions` / `actionBudget` type definitions — no change needed

## Related Work

- **Per-seat failure evaluation in competitive closing** (MS-0MUVQRBGY000LLR3) — blocked, related competitive mode work
- **Competitive turn orchestration in the scene** (MS-0MUTU8IYV0086PF6) — completed, established the seat-binding flow
- **Playable AI competitive mode (human vs AI)** (MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP) — completed, parent epic
- **Main Street: tutorial coverage for action banking** (MS-0MT3JK16W006A66P) — open, related to banking feature

# Provide reason for game ending

## Problem statement

When a run ends, the Game Over overlay does not make it clear **why** it ended
and, in competitive mode, does not surface the per-player state (coins,
reputation, score) that determined the outcome. Players are left guessing
whether they (or an opponent) went bankrupt, suffered a reputation collapse, hit
the score threshold, completed all challenges, or won by last-standing.

## Users

- **Human player (single-player)** — wants to understand the reason their run
  ended and see their final stats.
  - *As a player, I want the Game Over screen to state plainly why the game
    ended, so that I can learn from the run.*
- **Human player (competitive)** — wants to see every seat's final coin,
  reputation and score, and whether an opponent was eliminated (bankruptcy /
  reputation collapse).
  - *As a competitive player, I want to see all players' final state side by
    side, so that I understand how the win/loss was decided.*
- **Balance/content designer** — wants the end-of-run summary to be legible when
  reviewing playtests and screenshots.
  - *As a designer, I want the game-ending reason and per-seat state visible at a
    glance, so that playtest debriefs are faster.*

## Acceptance criteria
- **1.** **Two-column layout.** `showGameOverOverlay()` renders the panel as two labelled columns: a **left "Game State" column** and a **right "Summary" column**, with the title and end-reason headline spanning the top of the panel. Both columns fit within the existing overlay panel without text clipping or vertical overflow in the tested viewport.
- **2.** **End reason is explicit.** The headline states the game-ending reason in plain language derived from `state.endReason` (e.g. *Bankruptcy*, *Reputation collapse*, *Score threshold reached*, *All challenges completed*, *Last standing*, *Turn limit exhausted*), and names the player concerned when the reason is a per-seat failure (competitive mode).
- **3.** **Left column — all players.** The left column lists every player. For each player it shows coins, reputation and score, using the existing seat labels (`You` for the human seat, `AI <n>` for AI seats) and reading each `PlayerRecord` directly (not the shared scratch bank). In single-player the single player row is shown.
- **4.** **Left column — challenges met.** The left column shows the run's completed challenges (and/or the active-challenge completion state), so the player can see which challenges were met. *(Assumption: challenges are run-global in the engine — see Open Questions.)*
- **5.** **Left column — elimination/failure indicators.** A player who is bankrupt (`coins < 0`), has a reputation collapse (`reputation <= 0` after turn 1), or is marked `eliminated` is clearly flagged (e.g. a "Bankrupt", "Reputation collapse" or "Eliminated" badge) next to that player's row.
- **6.** **Right column — retained summary.** The right column preserves the existing summary detail from the current screen: score breakdown (coins, reputation, challenges, final score), challenge details, tier-unlock notifications, current tier + campaign stats, the difficulty selector, and the `[ Play Again ]` / `[ Menu ]` buttons — repositioned into the right column.
- **7.** **Both modes.** The overlay works in single-player (no `state.players`) and in competitive mode (`state.players` present), with the competitive scoreboard model (`buildCompetitiveScoreboard`) reused for the per-player rows where possible.
- **8.** **Testing/validation.** New tests cover the end-reason headline text for each `EndReason`, the per-player row content, and the failure/elimination indicators; existing game-over browser/animation tests continue to pass.
- **9.** **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **10.** **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
## Constraints

- **Presentation only.** No engine/state mutations; the overlay reads committed
  state only. Headless/replay mode (`scene.replayMode`) must remain exempt.
- **Overlay conventions.** Use `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`
  from `@ui`; parent all elements into `s.hudContainer`; keep the depth
  convention (199 backdrop / 200 box / 201 interactive); push everything into
  `s.overlayObjects` for dismissal.
- **Reduced-motion safe.** The overlay itself adds no animation (existing
  `animateGameOver` feedback is unchanged).
- **No new card art / audio assets** required.
- Panel size must remain readable at the existing game layout
  (`s.layout.gameW` / `s.layout.gameH`); the layout is currently a fixed
  500-wide panel — widening/reflowing is in scope but must not regress existing
  overlays (e.g. Manage Card, undo-challenge dialog).

## Existing state

- The Game Over overlay is implemented in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` → `showGameOverOverlay()`; it already
  shows the title (`You Win!` / `Game Over`), the raw `endReason` with
  underscores replaced by spaces, a centred score breakdown, per-challenge
  details, tier-unlock notifications, campaign stats, a difficulty selector and
  the Play Again / Menu buttons.
- The end reason is stored on `state.endReason` (`EndReason` union in
  `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`) and the winner in `competitiveWinnerId`.
- Competitive seat display already has a pure, unit-tested model:
  `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`
  (`buildCompetitiveScoreboard`, `formatCompetitiveScoreboardRow`) with `You` /
  `AI <n>` labels.
- Per-seat failure semantics are defined in
  `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` (`checkCompetitiveSeatFailure`,
  `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`, `eliminateCompetitiveSeat`,
  `checkLastStanding`).
- `PlayerRecord` (in `MainStreetStateTypes.ts`) carries `coins`, `reputation`,
  `score`, `controller`, `aiStrategy`, `eliminated`.
- Browser test harness pattern exists in
  `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts` and
  `tests/main-street/MainStreetOverlay.browser.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Redesign `showGameOverOverlay()` into a two-column panel:

- **Top band:** title (`You Win!` / `Game Over`) + an explicit, plain-language
  end-reason headline that names the failing player when applicable.
- **Left "Game State" column:** one row per player (label, coins, reputation,
  score, failure/elimination badge), followed by the challenge completion
  section.
- **Right "Summary" column:** the retained summary content (score breakdown,
  challenge details, tier unlocks, tier + campaign stats, difficulty selector)
  with the Play Again / Menu buttons anchored at the panel bottom.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Rewrite `showGameOverOverlay()` into
  the two-column layout; add an end-reason label helper and per-player row
  rendering.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts` — Reuse/extend
  `buildCompetitiveScoreboard` (and/or a new pure formatter) to feed the left
  column; may need a failure/elimination flag on the row model.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Reference `EndReason`, `PlayerRecord`,
  `competitiveWinnerId` (read-only; likely no change).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — Reference-only: per-seat failure and
  last-standing semantics (likely no change).
- `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts` — Extend for two-column layout

- `tests/main-street/competitive-hud.test.ts` or a new
  `tests/main-street/game-over-summary.test.ts` — Pure unit tests for the
  scoreboard/end-reason formatting used by the overlay.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — Document the new Game Over layout.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** — *Playable AI competitive mode (human vs AI)*
  (completed) — introduced `PlayerRecord`, the competitive scoreboard and the
  competitive end conditions this overlay must explain.
- **MS-0MUVBH589001L7NL** — *Competitive game ends on AI seat failure —
  reputation collapse or bankruptcy (eliminate AI instead of ending human game)*
  (completed) — defines per-seat failure attribution shown in the left column.
- **MS-0MUVQRCQJ00737UV** — *Last-standing win + continue-solo option*
  (blocked, `plan_complete`) — adds `last_standing` /
  `last_standing_continue` end reasons the headline must render; also adds the
  continue-solo opt-in which may need a place on this overlay.
- **MS-0MTKQ8E5M0021WHW** — *Endless mode button in end-game dialog* (open) —
  also modifies the game-over dialog; coordinate layout changes to avoid
  conflicts.
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` §Competitive end conditions —
  authoritative description of competitive end semantics.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` §Game-over celebration / loss sting —
  existing game-over presentation contract.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MURO9SVW007YXH8** – Remap remaining 9 docs files + card-catalog-baseline.json (25 stale refs) (open)
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)

- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: along, bankrupt, challenges, clear, coin (+29 more)
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: along, bankrupt, challenges, clear, coin (+26 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: along, bankrupt, challenges, clear, clearly (+25 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** challenges are run-global (`state.activeChallenges` /
  `challengesCompleted`), so "challenges met" is shown once per run, not per
  player. *Risk:* if the producer intended per-player challenge attribution,
  the engine has no such data and a follow-up work item would be needed.
- **Assumption:** priority `critical` (as set on the item) is intentional;
  classification guidance would otherwise suggest `high` for a UX clarity
  improvement. Not changed without operator confirmation.
- **Layout risk:** a fixed 500 px panel is already dense; adding a second column
  may require widening the panel, which risks overlap on smaller viewports.
  Mitigated by browser tests asserting no clipping.
- **Scope creep:** "richer end-of-run statistics" / post-game analytics are out
  of scope — record as linked work items instead.
- **Regression risk:** the overlay is shared with tier unlocks and campaign
  stats; restructuring must not drop the existing meta-progression display.
- **Coordination risk:** `MS-0MTKQ8E5M0021WHW` (endless-mode button) and
  `MS-0MUVQRCQJ00737UV` (continue-solo) touch the same dialog.

- **Q (assumption, not asked):** Should the "challenges met" information be

  challenges live on `state.activeChallenges` / `state.challengesCompleted`, not

  **OPEN QUESTION** for the producer.
- **Q (assumption, not asked):** Does this apply to both single-player and

  to a single player row in single-player. Source: item description says "all
  players", and single-player is the N=1 case. **OPEN QUESTION** for the

- **Q (assumption, not asked):** Is the item priority `critical` intentional
  (guidance would suggest `high`)? — **Answer (agent, assumption):** retained as

- **Q (none asked, plan session 2026-10-06):** Were new clarifying questions required to decompose this item? — **Answer (agent):** No. The intake brief already carried 10 measurable acceptance criteria, a desired-change sketch, constraints and predicted key files; the decomposition into five test-first vertical slices was unambiguous, so the plan proceeded without an interview round. The three existing OPEN QUESTIONs (per-player vs run-global challenges; single-player vs both-mode scope; priority `critical` vs `high`) remain producer-directed but non-blocking. # Community Garden should be Entertainment

## Problem statement

The Community Garden community-space card (`cs-community-garden`) currently has a `Food` synergy type, but thematically and by producer decision it should be an `Entertainment` synergy card.

## Users

- **Player**: building an Entertainment cluster on the street should include the Community Garden as a synergistic anchor alongside Park, Playground, Arcade, Cinema and Music Store.
- **Balance owner**: tier-synergy balance must remain within the 2× ratio rule per tier.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data** — In `tce-main-street/src/card-data.csv` (row for `cs-community-garden`), change `synergyTypes` from `Food` to `Entertainment` (CSV column 6, currently `Food`).
2. **Card description** — Update the card's `description` column from "A shared garden plot for the neighbourhood. Costs 10 coins per turn to run and provides +10 reputation per turn." to a description that reflects Entertainment synergy (e.g. "A shared community garden that hosts seasonal flower festivals. Costs 10 coins per turn to run and provides +10 reputation per turn.").
3. **Test data contract** — Update `tce-main-street/tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` (line 56, `NEW_COMMUNITY_SPACE_CONTRACTS`) to reflect `synergyTypes: ['Entertainment']` for `cs-community-garden`.
4. **Card text / data consistency** — Run `card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` and confirm it still passes (no coin/reputation values in the description change; only semantic wording).
5. **Tier synergy balance** — Verify `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` still passes. T4 synergy counts change from Service 1, Food 2, Entertainment 1 to Service 1, Food 1, Entertainment 2 — both satisfy the 2× max/min ratio.
6. **Card catalog docs** — Update `tce-main-street/docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`:
   - Change the Community Garden row's synergy description from "Food reputation asset" to "Entertainment reputation asset".
   - Update the Synergy Type Coverage table: remove Community Garden from Food single-type count (4→3) and add it to Entertainment single-type count (5→6).
7. **Content design docs** — Update `tce-main-street/docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (community-space table row for Community Garden) to reflect Entertainment synergy.
8. **Build** — `npm run build` is green in the `tce-main-street` repo.
9. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Data is source of truth**: the synergy type lives in `card-data.csv`; all downstream tests and docs derive from it.
- **Integer economy**: no coin/reputation value changes — only the synergy type and description semantics change.
- **Save/challenge compatibility**: the card ID (`cs-community-garden`) does not change; synergy type is a data-only change with no structural impact on save states.

## Existing state

- `cs-community-garden` in `tce-main-street/src/card-data.csv` row 36: `synergyTypes = Food`, tier 4, ongoing cost 10, reputation per turn 10, cost 500.
- `group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` asserts `synergyTypes: ['Food']` (line 56).
- `card-catalog.md` describes Community Garden as a "Food reputation asset with a small running cost" and lists it in the Food single-type coverage (4 cards).
- `content-design-and-progression.md` table lists Community Garden with synergy "Food" at tier 4.
- `card-art-map.json` maps Community Garden art correctly — no change needed (art is theme-neutral).
- `card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — no coin/reputation values in description text, so it should pass unchanged.

## Desired change

One-line CSV edit + test contract update + three doc updates + verification that tier-balance and card-text-consistency tests pass.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tce-main-street/src/card-data.csv` — change synergyTypes column from Food to Entertainment; update description text.
- `tce-main-street/tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` — update `NEW_COMMUNITY_SPACE_CONTRACTS[1].synergyTypes` from `['Food']` to `['Entertainment']`.
- `tce-main-street/tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` — no change needed (T4 not snapshot-tested), but verify the suite still passes.
- `tce-main-street/docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — update synergy description and coverage table.
- `tce-main-street/docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — update Community Garden row in community-space table.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSQJ210I003ADIY** — Main Street: design 50+ new cards of varying types (the epic that introduced Community Garden with Food synergy).
- **CG-0MSQJ210I00491ZZ** — Group B: Community Space — expand the family (added Community Garden among 6 new community spaces).
- **CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB** — Per-tier synergy balance rebalance (Park retagged Culture→Entertainment; this change is analogous).
- **CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK** — Park should cost 0.4 per turn to maintain (precedent for community-space balance changes).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Balance impact**: changing Community Garden from Food to Entertainment shifts T4 from Service 1 / Food 2 / Entertainment 1 → Service 1 / Food 1 / Entertainment 2. Both configurations satisfy the 2× ratio, so no balance regression is expected.
- **Test coupling**: the `group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` contract test will fail if the CSV is updated but the test data is not — they are updated in the same change, so this is not a risk.
- **Scope creep**: adjusting other Food cards (Bakery, Delicatessen, Diner) or rebalancing tier counts are out of scope; record separately if needed.
- **Assumption**: no other code paths hardcode `"Food"` in connection with `cs-community-garden` — verified by search.

- Q: "Should Community Garden be Entertainment?" — Answer (producer): Yes, Entertainment. Source: operator directive (work-item title).
